jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship Sydney campus is uniquely Canva - an extension of our Surry Hills neighbourhood. It’s a thoughtfully designed space with plenty of room to collaborate, focus and connect.

This role is based in Sydney, and we’re looking for someone who calls it home. Our hybrid way of working gives you the flexibility to work remotely, and to come together on campus for meaningful in-person collaboration and connection when it matters most. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Owning a portfolio of Search accounts (SEM, PMax/Shopping, GAC, ASA, ChatGPT Ads) across your assigned markets, with full accountability for performance, campaign structure, and incrementality-informed budget decisions
  • Being the go-to Search expert for your markets, leading stakeholder communications and partnering with regional and cross-functional stakeholders, educating them on how Search works and what it's contributing to their market.
  • Going deep on your strategic focus areas, driving the global approach and strategy in that space
  • Using AI as your default workflow accelerant - propose, build and maintain shared automation or process improvements, especially where manual, repeatable work is slowing the team down
  • Supporting new market launches and major platform changes (eg. AI Max testing and rollout or responses to bidding algorithm updates), that affect the whole team's approach
  • Partnering with measurement/data and AdTech teams on measurement and experimentation plans, flagging signal or tracking issues and communicating fixes clearly
  • Staying ahead of platform and industry changes, including how AI is reshaping search, adjusting our strategy proactively

You're probably a match if

  • You've run Search & Shopping accounts at genuine multi-market scale, with meaningful budget, in-house or agency-side.
  • You're hands-on with Google Ads and Bing Ads, plus a bid management platform like SA360 or equivalent.
  • You use AI tools to speed up reporting, analysis, testing and workflow automation.
  • You have a natural curiosity for platform mechanics, auction dynamics and bidding algorithms, not just campaign management.
  • You can dive deep enough into the numbers to spot when something doesn't add up, and diagnose why.
  • You bring high attention to detail on account hygiene, structure, measurement setup and reporting.
  • You can prioritise across multiple markets and workstreams at once.
  • You communicate clearly with regional stakeholders who don't have deep Search expertise, translating technical mechanics into plain language.
  • You build relationships across regional teams without formal authority, and work closely with Search, measurement/data and AdTech partners.
  • You're comfortable working across timezones with a globally distributed team, including some evening calls for EMEA.
  • You thrive in fast-paced, high-ownership, ambiguous environments, turning a loosely defined brief into a concrete plan.
  • You're proactive by default, transparent about capacity and blockers, open to direct feedback, and you move at pace.

About the team

Canva's Performance Marketing Centre of Excellence sets global strategy and standards for paid channels including Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Programmatic, and Search, while country teams own local execution and creative.

The Search team sits within the Performance Marketing CoE and owns global strategy and execution for Search, which covers SEM, PMax/Shopping, Google App Campaigns, Apple Ads, and emerging AI-driven search surfaces like ChatGPT Ads. It's a small, technical team with points of contact covering North America, Europe, Latin America & South East Asia, working closely with regional marketing teams, measurement/data partners and AdTech teams. We move fast, work with a lot of autonomy, and build strong relationships across regions without needing formal authority to get things done. The bar isn't campaign management, it's genuine platform expertise, systems thinking, and the judgement to know what a metric is really telling you.

You'll report to the Search Lead, taking ownership of a portfolio of country accounts and key strategic pillars within the team. You'll work across genuinely large, global accounts, with an opportunity to shape the direction of how the team's newer surfaces (eg. AI Max, ChatGPT Ads) should be run, and a strong expectation that you bring craft expertise, systems thinking and automation to the table rather than just executing campaigns.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

jobDescription.text:
What you'd be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve. At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • You sweat the details — inconsistencies catch your eye and you hold yourself to a high quality bar even on repetitive tasks
  • You're self-directed and can manage your own time across multiple concurrent projects without needing to be chased
  • You're adaptable — you can pick up new guidelines quickly and apply them consistently across different task types
  • You're genuinely curious about AI and excited to be part of building language experiences that work for Italian users
  • You thrive in a fast-paced environment where the work evolves and no two weeks look exactly the same

Canva's Localisation team sits within the International Supergroup and is responsible for bringing Canva's product and AI experiences to users in their language, across the world. jobs.name: Staff Software Engineer - Video Performance - (Bay area only)

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hello, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

About the role:

Video is the most resource-hungry thing Canva does. Every layer of it costs something: the browser, the phone in someone's hand, the native engine underneath, on-device ML, and the backend pipelines behind all of it. As a Staff Software Engineer on the Video Performance team, you'll own how fast all of that actually feels.

This is a full-stack performance role, anchored in the client. You'll decide what good performance means for Video, build the measurement that makes it visible, then lead the work that moves the numbers. That work runs across web and mobile surfaces, our cross-platform Native Video Engine, the Effect Platform, on-device ML and the backend services behind them. Deep expertise in one of those layers is a good place to start from. What matters most is being able to follow a slow user journey wherever it leads, and leaving behind tools that let other engineers do the same.

Most of our users are on mid-range and older devices. Keeping the experience fast for them, while the group keeps adding AI features and high-fidelity effects, is the genuinely interesting part of this job.

What you'd be doing:

As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you a flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

  • Own performance across the whole video creation lifecycle: template load, media import, timeline scrubbing, real-time preview, playback, effects and export, on web, iOS and Android. When a bottleneck turns out to live in someone else's layer, you follow it there.
  • Define the performance metrics and service level objectives for Video, and make sure they track what people actually notice rather than what happens to be easy to measure.
  • Build the measurement layer underneath that: telemetry, tracing, dashboards, alerting and regression detection, plus the profiling and benchmarking tooling, traces, device labs and automated performance suites, so any engineer in Video can diagnose a slow path without waiting for you.
  • Ship measurable improvements to latency, frame stability, memory and battery life. Sometimes that means a product or pipeline change. Sometimes it means critical-path work in the native engine, the shaders, or the ML-powered effect pipelines, wherever the data points.
  • Work with the Native Video Engine, on-device ML and Editing teams to rework hot paths for better parallelism, caching, hardware acceleration and asynchronous processing, and get Video treating performance as a product feature rather than cleanup work.

You're probably a match if:

  • You count every millisecond, byte and milliamp, and you've made real systems measurably faster. You can talk through the numbers.
  • You've built at the client layer, on web, mobile or native, and you can follow a problem down into backend services or platform code when that's where the time is going. You find your bearings in an unfamiliar stack quickly.
  • You've built performance tooling that other engineers came to rely on: profilers, tracing and instrumentation, benchmarking harnesses, regression suites or telemetry pipelines. You're at home in tools like Perf, Instruments, Perfetto, Android Studio Profiler and Chrome DevTools, happy to build your own when none of them fit, and you can define a metric that means something, spot a regression and prove an optimisation worked with data rather than intuition.
  • You understand concurrency, memory behaviour and CPU and GPU cost models well enough to explain why something is slow, not only where.
  • You have a working understanding of video pipelines: playback, codecs, container formats, frame-accurate seeking and composition. Or the appetite to pick it up quickly.
  • You prioritise by user impact, starting with the journeys people use most on the devices that struggle most, and you can influence engineering teams you don't own, across time zones, to get that work landed.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on iOS or Android development focused on system-level performance (strongly preferred): UI responsiveness, startup, memory, battery and thermal behaviour, especially on low-end Android devices. Having built native apps, players or editors yourself counts for a lot here.

  • Proficiency in C++, or a comparable systems language such as Rust, optimising critical paths in a native engine, plus familiarity with graphics APIs (OpenGL, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU) and how rendering choices affect frame times.

  • On-device ML performance work, such as tuning inference latency with CoreML, TFLite or TensorRT, or WebAssembly performance tuning for heavy compute in the browser.

  • Contributions to open-source multimedia or graphics projects such as FFmpeg or Chromium.

About the team:

The Video Group is a global team of rendering engineers, ML engineers and product people, spread across Sydney, San Francisco and Beijing. In San Francisco you'd be joining a small team whose job is to keep the foundation solid while the rest of the group builds quickly on top of it.

We care about getting the details right, and we think an experience that feels effortless is worth a lot of unglamorous work underneath.

Where and how you can work:

Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under to a hub in San Francisco, which is now home to our US operations. We offer flexibility in how and where you work. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard, and we do, but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages, because we want our success to be yours too

  • Health benefit plans to support you and your wellbeing

  • 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents and carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup and more

  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge, and support you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

At Canva we value fairness, and we strive to provide competitive, market-informed compensation whilst ensuring internal equity within the team in each region. We make hiring decisions based on your skills, experience and our overall assessment of what we observed and learnt in the hiring process. The target salary range for this position is USD $262,000 to $329,000. When calculating offers, we make salary decisions based on market data and candidates' skills and experience.

Other stuff to know:

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills, merit and business needs, in compliance with applicable local laws.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva, so even if you don't feel like your skills quite match what's listed above, we still want to hear from you.

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hello, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.


Where and how you can work

Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under, to a campus in Austin, Texas which is now home to our US operations. This is a hybrid role in Austin, Texas, so you must be able to commute to our office 1-2 times a week. 

About the Team

This role sits within Canva’s GTM Operations team, which partners with Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships, Finance, Revenue Systems, and Data to build the operating system behind Canva’s B2B growth.

You’ll report to the Head of GTM Operations and work closely with the Head of AMER Sales and the wider global GTM Operations team. We are a practical, high-impact team that combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, helping Revenue leaders make better decisions, remove friction, and scale the business with clarity and discipline.

About the Role

As the strategic business partner to the Head of AMER Sales, you’ll help shape how Canva grows across the Americas. You’ll connect commercial strategy with disciplined execution, bringing the insight, planning, and cross-functional alignment needed to help the business scale. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between strategy and detail, challenge assumptions, and help Sales leaders make faster, better-informed decisions.

What you'll do

  • Strategic business partnership: Serve as the primary strategic partner to the Head of AMER Sales, supporting regional planning, execution, and decision-making.
  • Forecasting & performance management: Own the AMER forecasting and performance-management rhythm, including forecast rollups, risk assessment, scenario modeling, executive readouts, and action follow-through.
  • Business cadences: Lead core operating cadences, including pipeline inspections, deal reviews, QBRs, and performance reviews in partnership with AMER Sales leadership.
  • Performance visibility: Build repeatable views of AMER performance across bookings, pipeline, conversion, coverage, capacity, productivity, attainment, and key growth initiatives.
  • Performance diagnosis: Diagnose trends across segments, markets, customer motions, products, and routes to market, translating data into clear recommendations for leaders.
  • Planning & resource allocation: Lead AMER inputs into annual and in-year planning, including headcount, capacity, territory and segmentation design, account assignment, productivity assumptions, and investment cases.
  • Cross-functional partnership: Partner with Finance, central GTM Operations, Revenue Systems, and Data to represent AMER in company planning and ensure trusted data for decision-making.
  • GTM efficiency: Identify structural opportunities to improve pipeline quality, deal velocity, coverage, efficiency, and predictability across the AMER sales motion.
  • GTM model evolution: Help evolve the AMER go-to-market model as the business scales, including the right balance of direct, Customer Success, partner, and reseller motions.
  • Global-to-regional execution: Bring regional insight into global GTM design while driving adoption of global commercial policies, processes, and standards.
  • Executive advisory: Act as a trusted advisor to AMER Sales leaders, balancing operational rigor, commercial pragmatism, and speed.
  • Executive communication: Translate complex data into clear narratives, insights, and recommendations for senior stakeholders.

What we're looking for

You’re a strategic, analytical thinker who knows how to turn complexity into clarity. You are equally comfortable advising senior Sales leaders and rolling up your sleeves to dig into a forecast, pressure-test a pipeline, or build a model from scratch.

You understand what it takes to build a predictable, scalable sales motion. You can spot risk early, identify the levers that will improve performance, and turn insight into a clear story and action plan. You thrive in complex, fast-moving environments and enjoy bringing structure to ambiguity without adding unnecessary process.

Most importantly, you are a trusted partner who combines analytical depth with strong business judgment and a practical, people-first approach. You are energized by helping teams operate better and building systems that scale as the business grows.

  • Experience: 7+ years in Sales Strategy, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or GTM Strategy, ideally in a high-growth B2B SaaS environment.
  • Leadership partnership: Proven ability to act as a strategic thought partner to senior Sales or Revenue leaders and translate insights into action.
  • Planning and commercial design: Experience with annual planning, territory and capacity planning, segmentation, account coverage, productivity modeling, and investment cases.
  • Forecasting and performance management: Deep experience with forecasting, pipeline health, scenario modeling, conversion, coverage, capacity, and attainment.
  • Analytics: Exceptional analytical and modeling skills, with advanced Excel/Google Sheets capabilities; SQL is required.
  • Business judgment: Strong instincts for balancing operational rigor, governance, and speed, with the ability to distinguish symptoms from root causes.
  • Influence: Clear, confident communicator who can influence across Sales, Customer Success, Finance, GTM Operations, Revenue Systems, and Data without direct authority.
  • Hands-on: Energized by ambiguity and comfortable moving between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.
     

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll also experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity, and fun woven throughout life at Canva. We also offer a range of benefits designed to set you up for success, both in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages — we want our success to be yours too
  • Health benefits plans to support you and your wellbeing
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents and carers
  • Annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup, and more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge, and support you personally

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills, merit and business needs, in compliance with applicable local laws.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hello, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under, to a hub in San Francisco, which is now home to our US operations. We offer flexibility in how and where you work. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

About the role

We’re looking for an experienced sales compensation leader to own the systems, data, reporting, and quarterly operating rhythm behind our global sales incentive programs. This role sits at the intersection of sales compensation, analytics, and technology. You’ll make sure our incentive platform is reliable, our compensation data is trusted, and leaders have a clear view of whether our plans are driving the intended outcomes.

This is a senior individual contributor role with broad ownership and influence. You’ll work independently, using judgment to solve complex problems and seeking guidance only in the most complex situations. You may mentor teammates and lead cross-functional work, but direct people management is not the primary focus.

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

At the moment, this role is focussed on:

Own the sales incentive platform

  • Act as the business owner for the incentive compensation platform, including configuration, data flows, integrations, access, releases, vendor management, system performance, and issue resolution.
  • Translate plan mechanics into accurate, scalable, and auditable system logic. Own requirements, testing, production validation, and change control.
  • Build and prioritize the platform improvement roadmap across stakeholder needs. Simplify complex processes and solve new problems where established solutions do not exist.

Own compensation data and payout readiness

  • Own compensation data from source through payout, including eligibility, assignments, quotas, territories, crediting, rates, tiers, accelerators, and payment outputs.
  • Lead recurring audits, reconciliations, and exception reviews. Proactively surface changes, risks, and root causes, then champion durable fixes.
  • Partner with Sales Operations, People, Data Engineering, Revenue Accounting, Finance, and Payroll to maintain dependable data flows and on-time commission processing.
  • Perform and validate complex or high-stakes sales compensation calculations.

Build reporting and plan health insights

  • Build the quarterly sales compensation QBR, creating a fact-based view of plan health, seller outcomes, operational performance, and emerging risks.
  • Analyze attainment distributions, pay-for-performance alignment, payout-to-revenue ratios, incentive effectiveness, payout concentration, ramp outcomes, exceptions, error trends, and performance by role, segment, and region.
  • Develop scalable dashboards and define the metrics, data structure, and quality standards needed for consistent decisions.
  • Turn analysis into a clear point of view and build executive-ready Canva decks that explain what happened, why it matters, and what leaders should consider next.

Run annual/quarterly plan delivery

  • Own plan setup, participant mapping, compensation letter generation, quality assurance, distribution, acknowledgement tracking, and final records.
  • Maintain accurate plan documents, rate tables, version history, and change logs.
  • Create practical materials that help sellers and managers understand how performance translates into payout.

Strengthen governance and scale

  • Maintain audit-ready documentation and management review controls across the end-to-end commission process.
  • Lead strategic projects and large-scale changes by setting clear outcomes, coordinating shared contributions, navigating competing priorities, and maintaining momentum.
  • Establish operating standards and repeatable processes that improve accuracy, timeliness, transparency, and accountability.
  • Use automation and AI thoughtfully while maintaining appropriate controls and human review.

You’re probably a match if

  • You have 8+ years of experience across sales compensation, incentive compensation systems, analytics, or related financial and operational work, with deep hands-on sales compensation experience.
  • You’ve directly owned or administered an enterprise incentive compensation platform and can move comfortably between plan mechanics, system configuration, data validation, and stakeholder needs.
  • You’re a strong analyst who can structure ambiguous questions, validate complex calculations, identify patterns, and connect findings back to business behavior.
  • You have advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills and experience with Tableau or Snowflake. SQL experience is strongly preferred.
  • You can build a compelling executive story from data and create clear, polished presentations. Experience using Canva is preferred, and a willingness to become highly capable in the platform is essential.
  • You understand sales compensation design and operations at scale, including quotas, crediting, eligibility, accelerators, guarantees, plan documents, controls, and payout processing.
  • You’ve led complex cross-functional projects with limited direction and can influence without formal authority, navigate differing stakeholder needs, and find common ground when decisions are high tension.
  • You bring strong judgment, curiosity, and ownership. You’re comfortable creating structure in ambiguity, helping others make sound decisions, and lifting the capability of people around you.

What success looks like

  • The incentive platform is stable, scalable, well controlled, and trusted.
  • Compensation data and quarterly plan materials are accurate, complete, and delivered on time.
  • Quarterly QBRs give leaders a consistent view of plan health and surface decisions early.
  • Complex cross-functional changes move from ambiguity to clear outcomes, ownership, and delivery.
  • Recurring issues are solved at the source, reducing manual adjustments as the business grows.


What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Health benefits plans to support you and your wellbeing
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

At Canva we value fairness, and we strive to provide competitive, market-informed compensation whilst ensuring internal equity within the team in each region. We make hiring decisions based on your skills, experience and our overall assessment of what we observed and learnt in the hiring process. The target salary range for this position is $181,000 to $260,000. When calculating offers, we make salary decisions based on market data and candidates' skills and experience.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under, to a hub in San Francisco, which is now home to our US operations. We offer flexibility in how and where you work. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

  • Own the North America social strategy and be one of the founding leaders of Canva's growing North America marketing function.

  • Build, lead, and grow a team of social experts and creators. Set the bar for great work, coach people up, and give them the ownership and trust to do their best work.

  • Widen where Canva shows up. Push beyond the current channel list (Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, YouTube, X, LinkedIn) into whatever platforms and formats earn real cultural relevance next.

  • Make social a source of ideas, not just an output. Feed what you learn from trends, culture, and audience reaction back into Canva's broader creative and marketing strategy.

  • Stay ahead of culture and platform shifts, and give the team a clear read on which moments are worth chasing and which aren't.

  • Partner closely with Partnerships and Communications so our biggest brand moments, talent relationships, and cultural bets show up seamlessly across earned, owned, and social.

  • Represent social in cross-functional rooms with marketing, product, and creative leadership, and make the case for why social deserves real investment and a seat at the table.

  • Own the North America social roadmap, budget, and reporting, and use performance data to know what to double down on.

  • Localize and adapt global campaigns so they land authentically with North American audiences.

  • Be the brand's guardian on social, keeping Canva's tone, values, and creative quality consistent even as the team moves fast and takes risks.

You're probably a match if

  • 8+ years in social media or brand marketing, with real experience leading and growing a team, not just running channels solo.

  • A track record of building social programs at a brand people actually talk about. Come ready to show the work and the results (follower growth, engagement, cultural reach).

  • Genuine cultural fluency. You're plugged into what's happening in American culture, online and offline, and you have sharp instincts for what will resonate and what won't.

  • Experience partnering with Communications, PR, or Brand Partnerships teams to align social with the broader brand and comms strategy.

  • A leadership style that empowers people. You know how to hire well, coach hard, and get out of the way so your team can do great work.

  • Strong executive presence. You can pitch a bold, unproven idea to leadership as convincingly as you can jump into the comments yourself.

  • Data fluency. You can read performance data, pull out the insight, and use it to sharpen strategy.

If you want to build a marketing channel from a strong foundation into something much bigger and help decide what American culture thinks of Canva, this is that role.


About the team

Canva is going all in on North America. We're building out our marketing function in the region from the ground up, and we're looking to level up our creative and our presence here massively. Social is one of the biggest levers we have to do that, and we want someone who can pick it up and run.

This isn't a maintenance job. You won't inherit a channel list to manage; you'll get a mandate to widen how and where Canva shows up, from the platforms we're already on to whatever comes next. Just as importantly, you'll change how social works inside Canva. Instead of being the last stop where finished creative gets posted, social becomes a source: ideas that start in the comments, in a trend, in a format, and travel out into our broader creative and marketing work.

The bigger ambition is cultural, not just channel growth. We want Canva woven into American culture, not just visible in it. About the team

The Security Group protects Canva's systems and data from information security threats, across Application Security, Risk Management, Enterprise Security, and Threat Detection and Response. Internal Systems Security is the team inside that focused on Canva's own environment.

What you'd be doing in this role

The Internal Systems Security team secures the environment Canvanauts work in every day. Laptops, networks, identities, the SaaS tools everyone relies on, and now the AI agents doing real work alongside us.

Most of this work used to follow a playbook. That's no longer true. Canvanauts now run AI agents that act on their behalf, which is a very different security problem to a person at a laptop. One of the questions on our plate right now: where does the policy layer sit for MCP tool calls, when we want decisions made per action rather than per application, and evaluated fast enough that nobody notices them?

This is a Staff level individual contributor role. You'd set technical direction without managing anyone.

At the moment, that means:

  • Going out to teams across the business, working out where their real risks sit, and building the roadmap with them rather than handing them one.
  • Helping those teams turn on AI workflows safely, instead of being the reason they can't.
  • Reviewing new tools and agents before they land. We're the team that says yes, no, or yes with these settings.
  • Threat modelling newer patterns like MCP, agentic workflows and SaaS to SaaS integrations, then turning what you find into controls people adopt.
  • Setting the standards other teams build against, and automating the work so a multiplying workload doesn't need a bigger team.

You're probably a match if:

  • You go looking for problems. You can point to something you found yourself, got other people to care about, and saw through to a fix.
  • You can bring people with you. You've convinced an IT or engineering lead to take on something that wasn't on their roadmap, without a mandate.
  • You've done hands-on enterprise, corporate or internal security engineering, and built and run security services in production. Endpoints, networks, identity, SaaS estates.
  • You value concepts over tools. Knowing the tooling matters. Knowing why a control works matters more.
  • You write and review code to a standard other engineers trust, and you automate by default.

Nice to have

  • Security work across a broad enterprise, especially somewhere less obvious like marketing or sales.
  • macOS at fleet scale: device trust, posture signals, zero trust, certificate-based device attestation.
  • SaaS security posture: configuration baselines, SSPM, OAuth and third party integration risk, non-human identities.
  • Securing AI agents, MCP servers or agentic workflows. Action level policy, tool call mediation, audit trails and containment.
  • Terraform, Python or Go, and cloud in AWS or GCP.

You will be part of a small but powerful UK team and there will be lots of opportunities to collaborate with many other specialities beyond localisation so we value energy and adaptability over specific experience or years of experience.

Every month, more than 100 million Canva users create a design in one of the 100 languages other than English, that Canva supports. The Localisation specialty is a small team of linguists, project managers, and engineers distributed throughout the company.

As a Product, Localisation and Growth Partner for the UK, you'll bring your product experience, cultural knowledge to all aspects of Canva for UK users, ensuring our users have the best possible Canva experience.

You will be the voice of UK users and the champion for culturally relevant content. Ultimately, you’ll be leading the charge in Empowering UK to Design!

  • Identify key opportunities for localisation improvements for the UK market

  • Identify and fix product funnel problems through signups, authentication, all the way to editing and publishing

  • Collaborate with the UK team on Product Growth initiatives

  • Tailor content for the nuances of the UK market

  • Work closely with local partners to ensure clarity, tone, and cultural nuance across all surfaces

  • Partner with internal stakeholders to develop language style guides, tone of voice strategies and localisation best practices

What we're looking for
You understand the needs of UK customers and the opportunities to meet those needs effectively.

You have proven product management experience, including owning product strategy and working in cross-functional teams.

We’re also looking for someone with tertiary experience in conversion rate optimisation seeing as the job entails improving the success rates across all of our landing pages and user workflows for the UK user.

We’re open to candidates from a range of backgrounds, and valuable experience could include product, growth, localisation or internationalisation work, and/or content design. Previous experience working for a SaaS or technology company is also highly valued.

You’re passionate about language and culture and you understand how these can impact local users’ experience of a product. Above all else, you care deeply about creating experiences that feel natural and intuitive so that Canva resonates with UK users and feels like home for them. Your analytical mindset helps you evaluate campaign effectiveness and recommend data-driven improvements for optimising user experiences.

You thrive in flat, collaborative environments where ideas can come from anywhere and success is a shared effort. You also love taking things from chaos to clarity. You’re a natural at understanding ambiguous, complex problems and communicating them simply to others. You also have the drive to see things through despite changes and setbacks. You’re equally comfortable discussing detail with engineers and ideas with product managers and designers. You’re great with tech (Atlassian project management tools, basic web development) and you write a mean doc.

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!
Thanks for stopping by. We know job ads can feel a bit formulaic sometimes, but we promise Canva is anything but. If you're drawn to what we're building and you see yourself in this role, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'd Be Doing in This Role
You'll join our Strategic Account Executive team within Canva Enterprise, working with named accounts on a global scale to help organisations consolidate design, content production and collaboration under one secure, centralised account. You're fluent in German and English, and comfortable moving between both with customers and internal partners.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Owning account planning — using a data-driven approach to identify and reach out to potential customers likely to benefit from Canva's products, analysing market landscapes, trends and dynamics to translate high-level plans into targeted sales activity
  • Managing pipeline and driving revenue growth — keeping pipeline, revenue forecasts and sales activity current in Salesforce for maximum efficiency and visibility
  • Leading with a customer-centric mindset — using compelling storytelling and vision transfer, presented through a creative lens, to guide customers on a journey that feels personalised and right for them
  • Being a genuine product expert — exhibiting a deep love for Canva's product and an ability to sell creative solutions that address customers' unique problems, while gathering customer feedback and market insight to help shape the Product roadmap
  • Fostering long-term relationships — building lasting partnerships both with customers and with internal cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering, Post-Sales, Customer Success)
  • Bringing chaos to clarity — simplifying complex situations into digestible, customer-ready stories and materials using Canva's own worksuite (presentations, docs and more)

You're Probably a Match If:

  • You're fluent in German and English, spoken and written
  • You have 8+ years of full-cycle selling experience across a range of customers, from medium-sized businesses to large corporations. For this Strategic role, we're looking for experience with large named accounts, ideally on a global scale within a technology company, with a demonstrated history of top performance
  • You have proven success managing a full sales cycle, including prospecting with a focus on new logo attainment
  • You're a pro at navigating complexity — understanding and addressing complex business challenges and crafting solutions to match
  • You've got a talent for creating detailed plans that cover all the bases within intricate organisations
  • You've got the skills to captivate an audience, especially in face-to-face meetings with multiple key stakeholders
  • You've got a track record of leading successful, complex negotiations
  • You're comfortable navigating uncertainty and can keep up in a fast-paced environment

About the Team
You'll be joining Sales & Success, the team behind Canva's go-to-market engine, supporting Canva Enterprise with the mission to empower every organisation to design. Canva Enterprise lets organisations consolidate design, content production and collaboration tools under one secure and centralised account — from whiteboards to docs, to presentations and our AI platform Magic Studio. We work with colleagues across the board, from Product to Marketing, all in support of our sales team. As we branch out into new markets and develop fresh Enterprise solutions, we're crafting something truly unique. Together, we're redesigning work.

What's in It for You?
Canva has grown hugely over the last few years, but we're only just getting started. Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages — so you share in Canva's success
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and support you personally

Other stuff to know
We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.
We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva, so even if you don't feel like your skills quite match what's listed above — we still want to hear from you!
Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship Sydney campus is uniquely Canva - an extension of our Surry Hills neighbourhood. It’s a thoughtfully designed space with plenty of room to collaborate, focus, and connect.

This role is based in Sydney, and we’re looking for someone who calls it home. Our hybrid way of working gives you the flexibility to work remotely, and to come together on campus for meaningful in-person collaboration and connection when it matters most. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

We are currently looking for a Corporate Accounting Manager to join our team.

We are looking for someone who thrives under constant change and is continuously looking for process improvements. Areas you would cover could include cash, intercompany, leases, accruals, and acquisition integrations. In this role, you’ll be a mix of reviewer and preparer depending on the level of complexity.

Additionally, in this role you’ll be expected to represent the corporate accounting team during AU hours by working closely with the broader accounting teams, tax team, and key business partners to support the close process, troubleshoot issues, and ensure accounting outcomes are accurate and reliable. As needed, you may also support adjacent initiatives such as systems enhancements, process documentation, and other accounting projects that strengthen close operations.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Corporate Accounting Lead, you'll play a pivotal role in strengthening Canva's month-end close capabilities while building a high-performing team that can support the scale and complexity of a rapidly expanding company.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Leading, coaching, and developing local corporate accountants, including performance management, career development, and building team capabilities.
  • Partnering with cross-functional stakeholders as needed to resolve month-end close issues, clarify accounting treatment, and support operational continuity.
  • Managing the integration of accounting processes and systems for acquired entities, ensuring seamless consolidation.
  • As needed - completing other general month-end close activities, including journals, reconciliations, flux analysis, and other close support as needed.
  • Maintaining effective internal controls and clear documentation to support accurate and timely close deliverables.
  • Identifying process improvements that strengthen close efficiency, accounting accuracy, and overall team effectiveness.
  • Supporting broader accounting projects and system enhancements that improve scalability and consistency across the close process.

You're probably a match if

You are a strategic Corporate Accounting Manager with strong technical expertise, operational skills, and a proven record of successfully developing and scaling accounting processes.

  • Proven experience managing and developing high-performing accounting teams with strong coaching and mentorship skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with FP&A, business leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • You are a strong team player with a proven track record of thriving on high-performing teams and continuously supporting a culture of growth and development through knowledge sharing and finding innovative solutions to complex problems.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, you are able to adapt quickly to changing circumstances and effectively navigate competing priorities.
  • You play a key role as a subject matter expert to support effective collaboration with cross functional teams and help drive business process transformation and change management.
  • You have extensive experience in establishing and standardizing policies, processes, procedures and controls that are SOX compliant.
  • Proficiency with Netsuite or other Enterprise ERP and adjacent tools
  • Nice to have - experience with Floqast, AI tools, Canva, and working on a accounting global team

About the Team

As Canva continues to rapidly grow, we are exposed to a broader range of external stakeholders, regulators, and reporting requirements. Joining a global team, the Corporate Accounting team is responsible for managing the close process, ensuring the accuracy, integrity, and transparency of financial information for all our stakeholders.

What’s in it for you

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity, and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

At Canva we value fairness, and we strive to provide competitive, market-informed compensation whilst ensuring internal equity within the team in each region. We make hiring decisions based on your skills, experience and our overall assessment of what we observed and learnt in the hiring process. When calculating offers, we make salary decisions based on market data and candidates' skills and experience.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship office is in Sydney, Australia, but we've made our way from down under, to a hub in San Francisco, which is now home to our US operations. We offer flexibility in how and where you work. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

About the Team

We’re building the partner ecosystem that powers how Canva shows up in the world. The Ecosystem Partnerships and Go-To-Market team sits at the intersection of product, growth, and platform strategy, working with the world’s most influential technology companies to unlock new value for Canva users. This team oversees the lifecycle of partnerships and developer community that brings innovation into Canva and into the 3rd party tools that our users rely on.

We believe the best products are built together, and we collaborate deeply across Canva to turn partnerships into meaningful user experiences and scalable growth engines. Our work directly supports Canva’s mission to empower the world to design by making Canva seamlessly connected to the tools marketers and creators already use every day.

About the Role

As a product partnerships lead, we’re trusting you to define and lead Canva’s strategy with key AI platforms and platform partners, including Anthropic, Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Meta, AWS, Notion, agent-centric platforms, and more.

You’ll own senior-level relationships, set long-term partner strategy, and turn those partnerships into tangible product and go-to-market outcomes. We work cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Legal, PR, Sales, Solution Engineering. and Operations to launch integrations, improve user experiences, and scale adoption and joint GTM success. You will shape the evolution of Canva’s product and platform - including the Apps SDK, Connect API, and other extensibility surfaces - ensuring that it meets the needs of developers, partners, and users.

This role has real scope, visibility, and impact — and is ideal for someone who loves a combination strategy, product, business development, partnerships, and growth. You will own partner and developer performance outcomes, such as active users for partner apps and integrations, partner-influenced revenue, and penetration among customer segments.


What you'll do

• Define and execute Canva’s AI technology partnership strategy, balancing long-term vision with near-term impact
• Lead complex partner engagements end-to-end, from strategy and negotiation through launch and scale
• Foster win-win partnerships that create value for Canva users and our partners alike
• Maintain deep, active relationships with partners, proactively resolving business and technical challenges
• Work cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Design, Solutions Engineering, Marketing, Legal, PR, Sales, and Operations to launch and scale partnerships
• Analyze qualitative and quantitative performance data to inform roadmap decisions and strategic opportunities
• Act as an internal champion for partners and an external ambassador for Canva

What we're looking for

You’re a strategic thinker who loves building things with other people. You’re equally comfortable in executive-level conversations and rolling up your sleeves to get things done. You bring a rare mix of business judgment, product intuition, and relationship savvy — and you thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

You have a strong product mindset and instinctively think in end-to-end user workflows — from first touch, to activation, to long-term value. You know how to translate partner capabilities into great product experiences and scalable go-to-market motions, whether that’s through product-led growth, sales-led distribution, or a thoughtful mix of both.

You’re able to spot monetization and growth opportunities early, validate them with data and partners, and turn them into launches that drive real adoption and impact.

Most importantly, you’re energized by building things that scale — for users, for partners, and for the business.

• Leadership: Proven experience (10+ years) leading strategic, product-led partnerships in AI, collaboration, platforms, SaaS, and / or developer ecosystems
• Partnership: Exceptional relationship-building and presentation skills, from C-suite to working teams
• Influence: Strong ability to influence across product, engineering, marketing, and GTM teams
• Product and GTM: A thoughtful balance of technical understanding, product sense, and commercial acumen (product management experience is a big plus)
• Organizational: Highly organized and analytical, with experience using data to guide decisions
• Hands on: Comfortable operating as both a hands-on IC and a strategic leader
• GSD mindset: Energized by change, rolling up your sleeves, complexity, as well as building something that scales

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll also experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity, and fun woven throughout life at Canva. We also offer a range of benefits designed to set you up for success, both in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:
• Equity packages — we want our success to be yours too
• Health benefits plans to support you and your wellbeing
• 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution
• Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents and carers
• Annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup, and more
•Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge, and support you personally

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills, merit and business needs, in compliance with applicable local laws.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

At Canva we value fairness, and we strive to provide competitive, market-informed compensation whilst ensuring internal equity within the team in each region. We make hiring decisions based on your skills, experience and our overall assessment of what we observed and learnt in the hiring process. The target salary range for this position is $232,000 to $306,000. When calculating offers, we make salary decisions based on market data and candidates' skills and experience.

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte, 안녕하세요!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time-consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

While we support flexible, remote-friendly ways of working, for this role we’re focusing on Seoul so we can best support our teams and keep collaboration flowing.

What you’d be doing in this role

Creative Direction

  • Develop a compelling creative vision that delivers and executes against the Country Content Strategy Lead and Country Manager’s strategic priorities.

  • Collaborate closely with local Marketing, SEO, and Community teams.

  • Translate country and regional strategies into locally relevant campaigns.

  • Drive AI adoption in production and content innovation, supporting new product formats and emerging trends to keep creative outputs fresh and competitive.

Content Creation & Curation

  • Oversee the creation of content, including design kits, campaign documents, creator briefs, and in-house production where needed.

  • Work with Freelance Copywriters and/or AI Copy to ensure copy is culturally relevant and adheres to our copy best practice standards.

  • Curate and editorially frame content for marketing initiatives, showcases, and seasonal calendars to elevate local relevance.

  • Proactively identify content gaps and curate assets that reflect strategic priorities and creative excellence.

  • Lead quality control of all content outputs, ensuring alignment with brand guidelines and maintaining high standards of visual and messaging quality.

Market Understanding & Cultural Insights

  • Build and maintain a deep knowledge of local culture, consumer behaviour, and design trends to inform content direction and strategy.

  • Conduct foundational content research, ensuring creative and editorial output aligns with strategic needs and cultural nuances.

  • Provide cultural expertise to scale content, ensuring authenticity and relevance to the local market across AICG, partnerships, and creators.

  • Champion hyperlocal design perspectives in collaboration with cross-functional teams.

  • Support building an editorial strategy for local content, ensuring Canva’s library reflects cultural relevance, diversity, and inclusive storytelling.

  • Advocate for the integration of global and underrepresented perspectives in content development and curation, upholding Canva’s commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

Content Performance Monitoring & Analysis

  • Conduct template and element audits to identify improvement areas and opportunities for new content.

  • Perform content performance and gap analysis, distilling insights into recommendations that guide future content creation and acquisition.

  • Leverage data, trends, and local insights to shape creative direction, enhance creator and in-house briefs, and inform design decisions.

  • Facilitate retrospectives and performance reviews to refine strategies and content effectiveness.

  • Actively raise discoverability challenges or product limitations that impact content visibility or engagement.

Partnership & Stakeholder Management

  • Partner closely with Country Content Strategy Lead, as well as collaborate with local SEO, Marketing, and Country Managers – to align on creative goals and content needs, and confidently prioritise and negotiate trade-offs.

  • Lead the rollout of local partnership content through culturally relevant creative strategies and campaigns.

  • Manage creative strategy, brand adherence, and feedback implementation to meet partner expectations and project goals.

  • Communicate initiatives and results to senior leadership, ensuring visibility across stakeholders.

Competitive Analysis

  • Monitor competitor activity and creative trends across the region to identify new opportunities and maintain strategic edge.

  • Use findings to inform the content roadmap and differentiate Canva's creative offerings in the local market.

Project Management

  • Monitor project execution, mitigate risks, and escalate challenges when necessary to ensure timely, high-quality outcomes.

  • Maintain visibility into campaign timelines and production volume goals across all creative operations.

  • Maintain an agile mindset and adapt quickly to shifting priorities and dynamic day-to-day needs.

Freelance & Creator Management

  • Oversee local freelance designers, managing recruitment, briefing, output review, and development.

  • Build strong relationships with the Creators Production and Community teams, providing hyperlocal direction through well-crafted briefs and feedback loops.

  • Champion Creator-led content that resonates deeply with local audiences and reflects cultural authenticity.

Reporting & Communication

  • Report on the performance and ROI of creative campaigns, using analytics to guide and improve future content plans and outputs.

  • Keep senior management and regional stakeholders informed about key initiatives, learnings, and creative progress.

  • Ensure alignment and transparency through consistent documentation and communication.

Feedback & Quality Assurance

  • Provide timely feedback and approvals across creative workstreams, maintaining alignment with both business goals and creative standards.

  • Drive internal reviews and uphold quality benchmarks for all deliverables across content types.

Team Building & Culture

  • Contribute to and foster a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing regional creative team culture.

  • Promote continuous improvement through process optimization, retrospectives, and shared best practices.

  • Encourage creative excellence while ensuring inclusion, psychological safety, and alignment across diverse teams.

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
Qualifications

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Design, Marketing, Communications, or a related field

  • Proven experience in creative leadership roles, ideally with international, regional, or market-level remit

  • A strong portfolio showcasing exceptional design work and content campaigns that reflect cultural resonance and local user needs

  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (SEO, Growth, Marketing, Product)

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and storytelling skills

  • A results-focused mindset, balancing creative innovation with business and user goals

  • Experience managing freelancers and/or creators, with a focus on quality and alignment

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, evolving environment with an experimentation mindset

additionalInformation.title: Additional Information
additionalInformation.text:
The Country Design Lead will join the International Content Team, whose mission is to build the most valuable content library in the world. The team sits within the International Supergroup and partners closely with Content & Discovery, Marketing, SEO, and other in-market teams to unlock content-driven growth through high-quality, locally relevant templates and elements across graphics, photos, and video.

The team is focused on delivering content that is truly local at scale – ensuring everything published meets Canva’s standards for design craft, cultural resonance, and user value, while leveraging AI and scalable systems to increase speed and impact.


This role is responsible for driving the creative execution of content for the South Korea market, translating strategy into high-performing outputs that reflect local culture, behaviours, and trends. Working in close partnership with the Country Manager, Country Content Strategy Lead, and cross-functional stakeholders, the Country Design Lead plays a key role in delivering content that drives engagement, adoption, and growth.

Operating as a hands-on builder and AI-native operator, this role leads the creation and curation of locally relevant content across both elements (graphics, photos, video) and templates spanning social media, presentations, websites, and print. This includes leveraging AI to accelerate production, and continuously improving quality and performance through rapid iteration.

This role will also direct a team of local creatives to curate and elevate impactful, truly local content across both elements — such as graphics, photos, and videos — and templates spanning social media, presentations, websites, and print products. By fostering a culture of excellence and innovation, this role will play a vital part in achieving Canva’s mission of delivering a world-class, truly local design experience.

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

  • You'll design and maintain lightweight SDKs, dashboards, and CI/PR checks that surface key performance metrics (LCP, INP, CLS).
  • You'll embed OpenTelemetry standards and extend data pipelines that ingest billions of real-user events every day.
  • You'll partner with platform and infrastructure teams to ensure low-overhead metric collection, shipping reusable libraries, CLIs, and tools.
  • You'll launch "no-merge-if-slower" checks that statistically flag or block regressions, with developer-friendly diff reports.
  • You'll run end-to-end investigations to profile, reproduce, and eliminate systemic bottlenecks using Chrome DevTools, Lighthouse, and similar tools.
  • You'll mine real-user and synthetic data to surface high-ROI opportunities for fixes and improvements in the monitoring tools.

You're probably a match if

  • JavaScript frontend expertise – proven experience designing, building, and shipping rich JS/TypeScript + React interfaces.
  • Full-stack fluency – comfortable diving into Node-based services and tools, data pipelines, and modern CI/CD workflows
  • Data-driven mindset – balance intuition with evidence, design statistically sound experiments, and let numbers guide your decisions.
  • Clear communicator – transform a flame-graph or p95 spike into an engaging narrative for engineers, PMs, execs, and other stakeholders.
  • Stakeholder influence – adept at working across multiple org levels, aligning priorities, and driving action in product, platform, and leadership circles.

Nice to haves:

  • Deep web-performance knowledge – expert understanding of rendering pipelines, main-thread bottlenecks, network protocols, and the latest performance APIs.
  • Large-scale observability & RUM experience – hands-on with Real User Monitoring, OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Looker, Mode, or similar systems processing millions of events per minute.
  • Strong TypeScript chops – proficiency crafting robust, typed code across both client and server.

Our ambition hasn’t changed since day one: make Canva the fastest graphic design platform on the planet. As a Senior Engineer in the Performance Monitoring team you’ll lead the charge—building tools, shaping culture, and guiding engineering practices so that brilliant performance is the default, not a nice-to-have. jobDescription.text:
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

What you'd be doing in this role

As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

You'd be the second Staff Engineer on Export, splitting the domain with our existing Staff Engineer so neither of us is a single point of failure on the hardest parts of the system.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Owning the technical direction of how Canva renders designs into files, including our Chromium-based export pipeline, and setting the architecture that keeps it reliable as both Canva's editor and Chromium itself keep moving
  • Being the person the team turns to on the hardest rendering problems: upgrade breakages, rendering race conditions, and production incidents caused by upstream Chromium changes
  • Deciding how we absorb upstream change rather than react to it, which covers monitoring and testing infrastructure that catches Chromium regressions before users do, and designs that survive Chromium's frequent output structure changes
  • Setting the direction for PDF accessibility and compliance (PDF/UA, WCAG) across exported files for our Enterprise customers, and making the calls on how deeply we tag, where we draw the line, and what we build versus buy
  • Leading on export reliability and performance at the scale of over 50 million weekly downloads, spanning format optimisation, distributed systems design, and the failure modes that only show up at that volume
  • Raising the level of the engineers around you through design review, pairing on gnarly debugging sessions, and the kind of documentation that turns one person's Chromium knowledge into the team's
  • Working across the Editing Platform group and beyond it, so that teams shipping new editor features know their work will hold up when someone hits download

You're probably a match if

  • You have deep experience with Chromium or another browser rendering engine, and you've worked inside it rather than just around it
  • You're comfortable in C++ when a problem takes you into a large third-party codebase, and you can build a clear picture of code you didn't write
  • A background in rendering pipelines, graphics programming, or print production systems
  • You're a strong Java backend engineer, that's what our product is built on
  • You've owned a technical domain end to end: you set the architecture, made the trade-offs, and lived with the consequences
  • You've debugged layered systems where the problem spans multiple codebases and languages, and you've led others through that kind of investigation
  • You bring the engineers around you along with you, through mentoring, design review, and the standards you hold
  • You've built or maintained systems where upstream dependencies change frequently, and you have a view on how to make that sustainable

Nice to have:

  • PDF specification knowledge, or experience with PDF generation and post-processing
  • Experience with accessibility standards in document or file output

About the team

The Export team sits within the Editing Platform group and owns one of Canva's most critical workflows: transforming designs into downloadable files that users can share, print, and bring to life. Over 50 million people download their creations through us every week. We focus on three things: reliability users can count on, speed that keeps pace with their creativity, and flexibility across every format and use case.

Beyond the main download flow, we power print production, enable AI model training, generate thumbnails, and make sure every new editor feature works seamlessly when someone hits that download button. As a Staff Software Engineer here, you'd be shaping how one of Canva's highest-leverage systems evolves, and the decisions you make will be felt by every team that ships something a user needs to download.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora,你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point. 

What you'd be doing in this role:

Canva is making experimentation a much bigger part of how we build and ship product.

At our scale, shipping changes and watching what happens isn't enough. Teams need to know whether a change actually improved the product and catch changes that unexpectedly hurt important guardrails such as retention or application performance.

This Staff Software Engineer will provide senior technical leadership across the backend systems behind Canva's experimentation programme.

You'll help evolve the platform teams use to set up experiments, target users, expose variants and measure outcomes in the safest and most intuitive way possible. We're moving towards a platform that does more than report results. It should reinforce good experimentation practices, surface signals faster and alert early when things go wrong.

With the advent of AI, we’re also looking at how we can automate more of the analysis process to help our teams learn faster and iterate.

You'll take ownership of significant technical problems, work with senior leaders across Canva and help shape where the platform should go next by working with the teams building the platform.

You’re probably a match:

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience:

  • Backend platform engineering: You've built backend systems or platforms that other engineers depend on, and understand what changes when your software becomes part of somebody else's critical path.

  • Experimentation exposure at scale: You've built, operated or worked deeply with experimentation, A/B testing, feature-management or progressive-rollout systems in a large engineering environment.

  • Technical leadership: You've taken ambiguous engineering problems, formed a technical direction and helped other engineers move towards an outcome.

  • Driving adoption: You've built internal platforms or capabilities and understand that the technology only succeeds when other teams trust and use it.

Technical knowledge:

  • Backend and distributed systems: Strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience designing reliable backend systems and reasoning about scalability, availability, consistency and failure modes.

  • Data systems: Enough familiarity with data engineering, analytics engineering or large-scale data processing to understand how experimentation data is generated, moved and consumed.

  • Experimentation concepts: Familiarity with experiment assignment, targeting, variants, feature flags, metrics, guardrails and progressive rollout.

  • Language depth: Java is our primary language and would be useful, but it isn't a hard requirement. At Staff level, we're more interested in strong engineering fundamentals and your ability to transfer them between languages.

Nice to haves:

  • You've built this before: Direct experience designing or building experimentation, A/B testing, feature-management or rollout infrastructure — either inside a large technology company or for a platform vendor.

  • Data crossover: A background spanning software engineering and data science, data engineering or analytics engineering.

  • Feature flags: Experience building feature flagging, user targeting, progressive rollout or automated guardrail systems.

  • Statistical intuition: You don't need to be a data scientist, but being comfortable enough with experimentation and statistics to work closely with one will be valuable.

About the Group & Team:

This role sits within Rollout Insights, the subgroup responsible for experimentation at Canva.

The team builds shared experimentation capabilities used across the company.

Engineers use the platform to configure and launch experiments. Data scientists use the resulting data to understand impact. Product teams use those insights to decide what should roll out, change or stop.

The team already brings together software engineering and senior data science expertise, which matters because the hardest problems sit across both disciplines.

You'll also collaborate broadly across Canva's engineering and data science organisations, including with senior technical leaders who depend on the platform.

Experimentation is now a major company priority, so demand for the team's capabilities is growing quickly. There's already a platform to build from, with plenty of important technical work still ahead.
