jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

What you'd be doing in this role

The Production Engineering team sits at the intersection of software engineering and the hardest reliability problems in Canva's infrastructure. At 240M MAUs, the hardest problems aren't on any product roadmap. Production Engineering exists to find them first and fix them properly. Writing software. Changing how production behaves. When it works, every team ships with more confidence and Canva gets faster and more resilient for the people who use it every day.

The strategic bet is a different model entirely. Canva's own take on what production reliability looks like, built for how we work. Senior software engineers embedded long-term in the areas that carry the most technical risk, working shoulder to shoulder with product teams, close enough to the roadmap to shape how features land in production before the problems compound. Not operationalising systems. Not running alerts. Writing software that changes how production behaves.

The engineers who do this work well have gone deep in systems most people only operate. They can walk into a codebase they didn't write, understand what's actually happening at scale, win the technical respect of the team they're embedded with, and then bend the software to make it more reliable, more efficient, and more resilient.

At Principal level, you're also the person who defines what this practice looks like at Canva. The calibration anchor for every hire, every engagement, and every standard the team sets.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Defining the engagement model: How Production Engineering pairs with product and infrastructure teams, how engagements are scoped, and what handoff actually looks like. This model is new. You're shaping it.

  • Leading the hardest engagements: Taking personal ownership of the most technically complex areas, sharding, multi-region architecture, JVM performance at scale, while the team builds depth in adjacent domains.

  • Setting the technical bar: What it means to be a production engineer at Canva. The standard for technical credibility. The archetype that future hiring calibrates against.

  • Pairing strategy across the team: Deciding how staff and mid-level engineers are paired and what they should be learning from each engagement. Growing production engineering capability across the org, not just within the team.

  • Connecting to the product roadmap: Working with engineering leadership across Canva to ensure Production Engineering is upstream of problems, not downstream. Influencing how product teams think about production readiness before they ship.

  • Building the measurement story: Incident severity and duration trending down. Feature launches going to production cleanly. You define what the metrics are and how they're tracked.

  • Compounding at organisation scale: One well-placed Production Engineering engagement changes how engineers build for years. At Principal level, your leverage is the sum of all those engagements, plus the standard you set for how each one runs.

  • What success looks like: As a secondee, developing trusted relationship with your team. Guiding them towards, shipping at velocity, with more confidence and less toil.

You’re probably a match

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience

  • Production at scale: You've owned reliability in large-scale distributed systems. When things went brake, you investigate how and shipped the solution that lasts forever.

  • Technical leadership in embedded models: You've led or helped shape a function where engineers work across team boundaries rather than within a single one. You know what makes that model work and what makes it fail.

  • Hands-on through seniority: You've stayed close to the code. At this level, you're the engineer others consult when the problem is genuinely hard.

  • Cross-org influence: You've shaped how teams outside your own make technical decisions because your technical judgement is trusted.

  • JVM or systems depth: You've built real things in Java, Go, Rust, C++, or a comparable systems language at production scale. Language matters less than depth.

  • Distributed systems in practice: You've navigated sharding, replication, failure modes, and consistency tradeoffs in production.

Technical knowledge

  • Linux internals: You can reason about process scheduling, memory, I/O, and the network stack when a system misbehaves.

  • Distributed systems: You've navigated sharding, replication, failure modes, and consistency tradeoffs in production. As well as consistent hashing, leader election, consensus, backpressure, circuit breakers

  • Observability tooling: You've built the tracing, dashboards, and alerting that tells you what's wrong.

  • Containerisation and orchestration: Kubernetes in production, at the scheduler level.

  • Performance analysis: You've profiled JVM applications or systems-level processes and fixed what you found.

  • Cloud infrastructure: AWS in production, across the failure modes that matter at scale.

  • Incident response: You've been on-call and have opinions about what good looks like.

Nice to have

  • Enterprise SaaS background: You've done this specific kind of work at an org that's done it well. You know what "production engineering" means when it's not just a job title.

  • JVM internals: You've tuned GC and profiled threads in production.

  • Multi-region or sharding experience: You've been involved in a data store migration or multi-region architecture where getting it wrong was not an option.

About the Group and Team

Join the Production Engineering Group at Canva, where our mission is to make every system that powers Canva fast, reliable, and ready for the next scale. Infra owns the infrastructure layer that every other team builds on: compute, storage, networking, developer experience, and reliability.

The Reliability Platform subgroup is where Canva thinks seriously about the technical risk that comes with operating at hundreds of millions of users. It's a group with broad scope, from the tooling that helps teams run incidents well, to the engineering work that stops incidents from happening in the first place.

Production Engineering sits within Reliability Platform. A small team of senior software engineers embedded in Canva's highest-risk technical areas, working alongside the product and infrastructure teams who own those systems for a long-term engagements. When it works, other teams ship more confidently and the incidents that do happen resolve faster and hurt less.

What’s in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard — and we do — but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages — we want our success to be yours too

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

What you'd be doing in this role

This role leads Core, one of Production Engineering's two teams.

You'll lead a team of software engineers who own Production Engineering's services and take on broader engineering problems that cut across multiple teams and groups. Core complements our Embedded team: where Embedded tackles targeted problems inside other parts of Canva, Core can take the strongest ideas and turn them into capability that works more broadly across the organisation.

Your job is to help the team turn complex, sometimes loosely defined problems into focused engineering goals and get them delivered. You'll stay close enough to the technical work to challenge assumptions, understand trade-offs and help engineers make strong decisions, while giving them the autonomy to own the detail.

Core is still taking shape. Several in flight projects have carried over from Reliability Foundations, and as those roll off through the rest of the year, you'll help define the team's next phase by setting its focus, priorities and the problems Core takes on next. You'll also help shape how initiatives are structured and measured, and turn lessons from individual pieces of work into capability with broader reach and impact across Canva.

You'll also own the day-to-day health of the team: setting clear priorities, coaching engineers directly, creating psychological safety and helping their team develop organisational fluency and influence.

Looking ahead, this role will help build:

  • Reliable services at scale: Help Core's services and capabilities keep pace as Production Engineering grows and more teams come to depend on their skills and expertise.

  • Standards worth reusing: Turn lessons from individual problems and engagements into engineering practices and capabilities that can be applied more broadly.

  • A strong Core–Embedded loop: Build the feedback loops that let targeted learning from Embedded become reusable capability through Core.

  • Growing engineering depth: Coach engineers to take on increasingly complex technical and cross-team problems as Core's scope grows.

You’re probably a match

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience

  • Leading engineers: You've led software engineers through complex or ambiguous technical work and know how to coach people to grow their skills and autonomy.

  • Production exposure: You've worked in software environments where reliability, scalability and production risk genuinely mattered.

  • Delivery ownership: You've taken significant technical initiatives from understanding the problem through to delivery, including work spanning multiple teams.

  • Driving adoption: You've helped teams adopt new tools, practices or ways of working, even when they were busy or already had an established approach.

  • Engineering leadership: You can communicate technical trade-offs clearly, set direction without prescribing every decision, and create an environment where engineers can challenge ideas, learn and do their best work.

Technical knowledge

  • CS fundamentals: A strong grounding in computer science fundamentals, including concurrency, multithreading and data structures.

  • Language depth: Enough depth in languages such as Go, Python, Java or C++ to engage meaningfully with designs, implementation choices and technical trade-offs.

  • Systems knowledge: Strong working knowledge of system internals, networking and cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP.

  • Systems thinking: Comfortable reasoning through ambiguous problems spanning multiple components and constraints, with a strong understanding of system design, architecture and engineering patterns.

  • Reliability engineering: Familiarity with observability, capacity, failure modes and the operational characteristics of production systems.

  • Scale and criticality: Experience working in large-scale or high-criticality environments where reliability failures have meaningful consequences for users, systems or the business.

Nice to have

  • SRE/PE management: Prior experience leading Site Reliability Engineering, Production Engineering or a closely related function.

  • Infrastructure exposure: Experience with large-scale storage, CDN, networking or distributed infrastructure.

  • Growing technical leaders: A history of developing engineers who can coach others and take on increasingly complex work.

  • Function-building: Experience helping shape the scope, ways of working or identity of a technical team while it was still evolving.

About the Group and Team

Production Engineering sits within Canva's Reliability Platform subgroup, part of the wider Infra supergroup responsible for the foundations Canva's engineering teams build on, including compute, storage, networking, developer experience and reliability.

At more than 250 million monthly active users, Canva's hardest reliability problems increasingly span systems, teams and organisational boundaries. Production Engineering exists to help keep Canva reliable, efficient and predictable as that complexity grows.

It's primarily a software engineering function. Rather than operating systems from the sidelines or papering over problems with process, Production Engineers solve operational challenges through design and code.

The function is split into two teams: Embedded and Core.

Embedded works directly alongside teams across Canva on targeted, long-running engineering engagements. Engineers typically work in small groups, bringing Production Engineering expertise directly into some of Canva's most important technical problem spaces.

Core owns Production Engineering's services and works on broader, more federated problems that span multiple groups. Sometimes work discovered through an Embedded engagement comes back into Core, where the teams can work together to turn a targeted solution into capability that benefits more of Canva.

Core is designed to operate as a larger, more focused team than the distributed Embedded model, with a smaller number of shared goals and a strong emphasis on engineering execution.

Because Production Engineering is still taking shape, both teams are helping define what the function becomes: where it can have the greatest impact, how it partners with other teams, and how individual wins become lasting engineering capability across Canva.

What’s in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard — and we do — but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages — we want our success to be yours too

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and support you personally

Other stuff to know?

We see AI as a powerful amplifier of creativity and technology at Canva. We're evolving how we assess AI skills in our Technology hiring experience — you'll tackle interactive, real-time challenges that reflect the kind of work we do. In some interviews, you may also be asked to solve a problem using an AI tool to show how you approach challenges with tech by your side.

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture.

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva, so even if you don't feel like your skills quite match what's listed above — we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

Your job is to help the team turn complex, sometimes loosely defined problems into focused engineering goals and get them delivered. You'll stay close enough to the technical work to challenge assumptions, understand trade-offs and help engineers make strong decisions, while giving them the autonomy to own the detail.

Core is still taking shape. Several in flight projects have carried over from Reliability Foundations, and as those roll off through the rest of the year, you'll help define the team's next phase by setting its focus, priorities and the problems Core takes on next. You'll also help shape how initiatives are structured and measured, and turn lessons from individual pieces of work into capability with broader reach and impact across Canva.

You'll also own the day-to-day health of the team: setting clear priorities, coaching engineers directly, creating psychological safety and helping their team develop organisational fluency and influence.

Looking ahead, this role will help build:

  • Standards worth reusing: Turn lessons from individual problems and engagements into engineering practices and capabilities that can be applied more broadly.

About the Group and Team:

Production Engineering sits within Canva's Reliability Platform subgroup, part of the wider Infra supergroup responsible for the foundations Canva's engineering teams build on, including compute, storage, networking, developer experience and reliability.

At more than 250 million monthly active users, Canva's hardest reliability problems increasingly span systems, teams and organisational boundaries. Production Engineering exists to help keep Canva reliable, efficient and predictable as that complexity grows.

It's primarily a software engineering function. Rather than operating systems from the sidelines or papering over problems with process, Production Engineers solve operational challenges through design and code.

The function is split into two teams: Embedded and Core.

Embedded works directly alongside teams across Canva on targeted, long-running engineering engagements. Engineers typically work in small groups, combining senior technical leadership with engineers who can learn from the engagement and help carry that knowledge forward.

Core owns Production Engineering services and works on broader problems that cut across multiple teams or groups. When an Embedded engagement uncovers an idea worth applying more widely, Embedded and Core can work together to turn that learning into reusable capability across Canva.

Embedded is deliberately weighted toward senior technical talent. Production Engineers need to enter unfamiliar problem spaces, understand complex systems quickly and earn credibility with the engineers who already own them.

Because the function is still taking shape, the team is also defining its own identity: where Production Engineering can have the greatest impact, how it partners with other teams, and how individual wins become lasting engineering capability across Canva.

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard — and we do — but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Please note this is a 12 month contract and you will be paid a day rate. 

 

Join the team empowering the world to design

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, こんにちは, 你好, hallo, नमस्ते, 안녕하세요, hola, salut!

At Canva, our mission is to empower the world to design—and we’re growing fast across the globe. With over 250 million monthly active users in over 190 countries, we’re on a mission to make Canva the most loved brand in the world. To support this ambition, we’re building a world-class marketing team that’s deeply local, highly creative, and relentlessly performance-focused.

 

About the role

Content moves Canva, and ensuring our content is a driver of growth is crucial. Just as we invest in strong business, marketing, sales, and product leaders in our priority markets, we need an equally strong voice in content.

As the Sub-Saharan Africa Content Strategy Lead, you’ll partner closely with the Sub-Saharan Africa Country Manager to ensure Canva has the right strategic content from your country (or countries), owning content as a growth engine and adapting strategies to support MAU, retention, and revenue impact.

You’ll work closely with the Sub-Saharan Design Lead to deliver content that drives business outcomes. You’ll also champion local relevance and trends that make international users feel Canva is for them, and work closely with country teams (SEO, Localisation, Creators, Product, Marketing) and regional stakeholders to ensure local content delivers high value and measurable impact.

You’ll be coached and supported by a EMEA Content Strategy Lead, who will drive content strategy across the region.

 

What you’ll do

As a Content Strategy Lead, you bring expertise in strategy, content, business management, and cross-functional stakeholder management. In particular, you will:

  • Content Strategy & Execution – Prioritise and execute country content strategy and growth levers, owning content health and production for your country to drive relevance, scale, and business impact.

  • Content Quality & Relevance – Ensure that your country’s content meets Canva’s standards, resonates culturally, and supports strategic growth metrics.

  • Feedback & Insights – Gather input from sales, partners, and local peers to refine content strategies and enhance Canva’s country impact.

  • Discovery & Performance – Own your country’s content performance across discovery, editorial ensuring the right local content is surfaced through search, recommendations, and editorial, and optimised for engagement, activation, and retention.

  • Editorial & Trends Leadership – Execute your country’s editorial strategy across surfaces (e.g. Showcases), identifying and activating cultural moments in partnership with Marketing, Social and PR.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Act as a strategic partner to Country Manager and country peers to align priorities, unblock execution, and drive content-led growth.

  • Creator & Partner Engagement – In collaboration with your country community and partnerships managers, build relationships with local creators and partnerships to activate a thriving content ecosystem.

 

What we're looking for

We’re seeking a strategic thinker who thrives in fast-paced environments and can drive content impact within their market. They’ll take a pragmatic approach to content creation – working across multiple production streams (AIGC, creators, localisation, bespoke, and partnerships) to solve local content needs, improve efficiency, and scale what works.

This role requires someone who can combine strong strategic thinking with a deep understanding of their local market — translating regional direction into actionable country-level plans, and working closely with Africa Design Leads to bring these to life. You should be someone who naturally gravitates toward solving problems, enjoys working with data to inform decisions, and can build strong relationships across cross-functional teams.

The ideal candidate combines analytical rigour with cultural curiosity, demonstrating both the ability to shape country-level content strategy and to identify opportunities to scale what works through repeatable approaches, AI-supported workflows, and strong partnerships.

  • 3-5+ years of experience in content strategy, regional business strategy and operations, partnerships, or similar roles within high-growth content, media or marketplace global technology companies.

  • A deep understanding of content, trends, and aesthetics in your market (or markets), with a pulse on what resonates with local users.

  • A proactive, solutions-driven approach, capable of balancing strategy with hands-on execution.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with the ability to align cross-functional teams across regions.

  • Experience working in fast-moving, dynamic environments, comfortable with ambiguity and change.

  • Strong analytical skills to assess content performance and inform strategy adjustments.

  • A track record of successfully managing production workflows, partnerships, and/ or supporting and activating local creators.

  • Language skills and cultural knowledge relevant to your geographic market, with ability to work effectively across different time zones.

 

What you’ll learn and how you’ll develop at Canva

You'll gain deep exposure to all aspects of strategy and operations a high-growth technology company, from AI-powered content innovations to international expansion. Working closely with senior leadership across International and other supergroups, you'll develop advanced strategic thinking skills while learning how to scale operations and drive organisational change.

You'll get hands-on experience with one of the most complex content ecosystems in tech, working on problems that don't have playbooks yet, and partnering with cross-functional groups across Canva to find solutions that impact millions of users. This is a role where your decision making and leadership will directly influence strategy, and you'll see your recommendations come to life in our product and shape the future of design.

Through the Content Strategy speciality growth infrastructure and Canva’s professional development programs, you'll develop your sharp commercial instincts, data analysis proficiency, the ability to navigate ambiguity, and hands-on experience with emerging technologies. Most importantly, you'll work with people who are genuinely brilliant and kind, a rare combination that makes the hard problems worth solving, and sets you up for a career in strategy in the tech industry.

companyDescription.title: Company Description
companyDescription.text:
About the Group/Team

Canva’s mission is to empower the world to design. With over 220 million users already on board, we have a bold vision to reach 1 billion users. The CJKI Group is dedicated to this mission, pouring our hearts and souls into driving hyperlocalization. We strive to make Canva feel like a local experience in China, Japan, South Korea, and India, ensuring that our platform resonates deeply with users in these regions.


About the Role/Specialty

In this role, you will be at the forefront of shaping how millions of people in China experience Canva. You will own the product experiences at the heart of that journey, from a user's first encounter with the product through to the moments that keep them coming back. Grounding your decisions in user insight and data, you will determine what is worth building, define it with clarity, and see it through to launch alongside our engineering, design and data teams.

Bringing that product judgement together with strong delivery discipline, you will also drive a number of cross-functional initiatives from concept to launch. You will bring structure to complex, multi-team work — anticipating risks and dependencies, sustaining momentum across functions, and raising the standard of how our team plans, tracks and communicates its work.

You will also serve as a bridge between the CJKI team and Canva's global product teams, bringing local insight to global decisions and shaping global launches so they resonate with local users. Together, we transform ideas into reality, making a tangible impact on Canva's success and the creative journeys of millions.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
What you’ll do (responsibilities)

  • You’ll own the product experiences in your scope end-to-end — from building a deep understanding of Chinese user behaviour and pain points, to forming a clear view of what is worth building, to defining it in specs your team can act on. You’ll define the metrics that matter, design experiments that produce reliable answers, and decide what ships.
  • You'll bring structure to ambiguous problems and take accountability for the trade-offs you make. Where the right answer isn't obvious, you'll form a considered view, test it, and stand behind the result.
  • You'll drive cross-functional initiatives to timely, high-quality delivery, working across engineering, design, data and marketing. You'll raise risks early and keep stakeholders informed in writing. You'll also help raise the standard of how our team plans, tracks and documents its work.
  • You'll partner closely with Canva's global product teams. You'll represent the China context with evidence, shape global launches so they work well for local users, and drive alignment without direct reporting authority.

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
What we're looking for 

 

We're looking for someone who combines strong product instincts with the discipline to make complex, multi-team work happen. You should be comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, and equally comfortable holding a plan together when several teams depend on it.

Skills, Competencies, and Attributes:

  • Product Sense: You can work out what to build and why, not just execute a requirement someone else has defined. You can point to a product decision you made yourself and what came of it.
  • Structured Thinking: You break ambiguous problems down methodically, reasoning through edge cases before committing to a direction — and you pick up unfamiliar domains quickly.
  • Consumer Product Experience: 3+ years of product or closely related experience, including owning consumer (B2C) products end-to-end, with a deep understanding of Chinese users and the local landscape.
  • Data Fluency: You pull and interrogate your own data, design clean experiments, and combine quantitative signal with user insight to make decisions.
  • Program and Delivery Management: You can run several workstreams at once, hold a realistic view of scope, dependencies and timelines, and raise risks early with options rather than late with excuses.
  • Stakeholder Influence: You build trust quickly across functions and drive alignment without formal authority, keeping everyone working from the same picture.
  • Communication and Documentation: You write specs people understand on one read, keep work tracked, and keep stakeholders updated before they have to ask. Fluent English and comfortable working with teams outside China.

Nice-to-have

  • A technical background, or enough grounding to hold a substantive conversation with engineering.
  • Experience in growth or subscription domains.
  • Experience handling regional differentiation and localisation in a global product.

By bringing these skills and attributes to Canva, you will play a crucial role in driving our product initiatives forward and contributing to our mission of empowering the world to design.

additionalInformation.title: Additional Information
additionalInformation.text:
What the candidate will learn and how will they develop at Canva

  • Master Canva’s Magic: Dive deep into Canva’s product ecosystem and become a wizard at managing and optimizing a variety of exciting projects. You’ll get hands-on with the latest tech and innovative practices that make Canva a design powerhouse.
  • Project Management Ninja: Perfect your project management chops by planning, executing, and delivering high-quality projects on time. You’ll learn to juggle multiple tasks and ensure smooth collaboration across teams like a pro.
  • Market Research Guru: Sharpen your detective skills by gathering and analyzing market data. You’ll learn to uncover insights that drive strategic decisions and help shape the future of our product offerings.
  • User Experience Rockstar: Develop a knack for enhancing user experiences. You’ll work closely with our talented design and engineering teams to implement cool features and improvements that delight our users.
  • Stakeholder Whisperer: Become a master at managing relationships with various stakeholders. You’ll learn to communicate effectively, address concerns, and drive consensus on key project decisions. Plus, you’ll thrive in Canva’s fast-paced environment, always ready to tackle new challenges and grow both personally and professionally.

By joining Canva, you’ll not only help empower the world to design but also embark on a fun and rewarding career journey filled with endless opportunities for learning, growth, and making a real impact.

jobDescription.text:
Join the team empowering the world to design

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, こんにちは, 你好, hallo, नमस्ते, 안녕하세요, hola, salut!

At Canva, our mission is to empower the world to design—and we’re growing fast across the globe. With over 250 million monthly active users in over 190 countries, we’re on a mission to make Canva the most loved brand in the world. To support this ambition, we’re building a world-class marketing team that’s deeply local, highly creative, and relentlessly performance-focused.

 

About the role

Content moves Canva, and ensuring our content is a driver of growth is crucial. Just as we invest in strong business, marketing, sales, and product leaders in our priority markets, we need an equally strong voice in content.

As a GCC Content Strategy Lead, you’ll partner closely with the MENAP Country Manager to ensure Canva has the right strategic content from your country (or countries), owning content as a growth engine and adapting strategies to support MAU, retention, and revenue impact.

You’ll work closely with the MENAP Design Lead to deliver content that drives business outcomes. You’ll also champion local relevance and trends that make international users feel Canva is for them, and work closely with country teams (SEO, Localisation, Creators, Product, Marketing) and regional stakeholders to ensure local content delivers high value and measurable impact.

You’ll be coached and supported by a Regional Content Strategy Lead, who will drive content strategy across the region.

 

What you’ll do

As a GCC Content Strategy Lead, you bring expertise in strategy, content, business management, and cross-functional stakeholder management. In particular, you will:

  • Content Strategy & Execution – Prioritise and execute country content strategy and growth levers, owning content health and production for your country to drive relevance, scale, and business impact.

  • Content Quality & Relevance – Ensure that your country’s content meets Canva’s standards, resonates culturally, and supports strategic growth metrics.

  • Feedback & Insights – Gather input from sales, partners, and local peers to refine content strategies and enhance Canva’s country impact.

  • Discovery & Performance – Own your country’s content performance across discovery, editorial ensuring the right local content is surfaced through search, recommendations, and editorial, and optimised for engagement, activation, and retention.

  • Editorial & Trends Leadership – Execute your country’s editorial strategy across surfaces (e.g. Showcases), identifying and activating cultural moments in partnership with Marketing, Social and PR.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Act as a strategic partner to MENAP Country Manager and country peers to align priorities, unblock execution, and drive content-led growth.

  • Creator & Partner Engagement – In collaboration with your country community and partnerships managers, build relationships with local creators and partnerships to activate a thriving content ecosystem.

 

What we're looking for

We’re seeking a strategic thinker who thrives in fast-paced environments and can drive content impact within their market. They’ll take a pragmatic approach to content creation – working across multiple production streams (AIGC, creators, localisation, bespoke, and partnerships) to solve local content needs, improve efficiency, and scale what works.

This role requires someone who can combine strong strategic thinking with a deep understanding of their local market — translating regional direction into actionable country-level plans, and working closely with MENAP Design Leads to bring these to life. You should be someone who naturally gravitates toward solving problems, enjoys working with data to inform decisions, and can build strong relationships across cross-functional teams.

The ideal candidate combines analytical rigour with cultural curiosity, demonstrating both the ability to shape country-level content strategy and to identify opportunities to scale what works through repeatable approaches, AI-supported workflows, and strong partnerships.

  • 3-5+ years of experience in content strategy, regional business strategy and operations, partnerships, or similar roles within high-growth content, media or marketplace global technology companies.

  • A deep understanding of content, trends, and aesthetics in your market (or markets), with a pulse on what resonates with local users.

  • A proactive, solutions-driven approach, capable of balancing strategy with hands-on execution.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with the ability to align cross-functional teams across regions.

  • Experience working in fast-moving, dynamic environments, comfortable with ambiguity and change.

  • Strong analytical skills to assess content performance and inform strategy adjustments.

  • A track record of successfully managing production workflows, partnerships, and/ or supporting and activating local creators.

  • Arabic Language skills and cultural knowledge relevant to your geographic market, with ability to work effectively across different time zones.

 

What you’ll learn and how you’ll develop at Canva

You'll gain deep exposure to all aspects of strategy and operations a high-growth technology company, from AI-powered content innovations to international expansion. Working closely with senior leadership across International and other supergroups, you'll develop advanced strategic thinking skills while learning how to scale operations and drive organisational change.

You'll get hands-on experience with one of the most complex content ecosystems in tech, working on problems that don't have playbooks yet, and partnering with cross-functional groups across Canva to find solutions that impact millions of users. This is a role where your decision making and leadership will directly influence strategy, and you'll see your recommendations come to life in our product and shape the future of design.

Through the Content Strategy speciality growth infrastructure and Canva’s professional development programs, you'll develop your sharp commercial instincts, data analysis proficiency, the ability to navigate ambiguity, and hands-on experience with emerging technologies. Most importantly, you'll work with people who are genuinely brilliant and kind, a rare combination that makes the hard problems worth solving, and sets you up for a career in strategy in the tech industry.

At Canva, our mission is to empower the world to design—and we’re growing fast across the globe. The Spanish Design Lead plays a pivotal role in Canva’s mission to democratise design by ensuring content is truly local, culturally resonant, and of the highest design quality. Partnering closely with the Content Strategy Lead and cross-functional stakeholders, this role directs and delivers content – at speed and scale – that drives user engagement, content adoption, and revenue growth in the Spanish market. 

Aligned to Canva’s international growth strategy, this role ensures the creative direction, production, and curation of market-relevant content across templates and elements. The role bridges global vision with local market needs, ensuring cultural authenticity while meeting business objectives.

 

About the role

The Country Design Lead will join the International Content Team, whose mission is to build the most valuable content library in the world. The team sits within the International Supergroup and partners closely with Content & Discovery, Marketing, SEO, and other in-market teams to unlock content-driven growth through high-quality, locally relevant templates and elements across graphics, photos, and video.

The team is focused on delivering content that is truly local at scale – ensuring everything published meets Canva’s standards for design craft, cultural resonance, and user value, while leveraging AI and scalable systems to increase speed and impact.


This role is responsible for driving the creative execution of content for the Spanish market, translating strategy into high-performing outputs that reflect local culture, behaviours, and trends. Working in close partnership with the Spanish Country Manager, Content Strategy Lead, and cross-functional stakeholders, the Spanish Design Lead plays a key role in delivering content that drives engagement, adoption, and growth.

Operating as a hands-on builder and AI-native operator, this role leads the creation and curation of locally relevant content across both elements (graphics, photos, video) and templates spanning social media, presentations, websites, and print. This includes leveraging AI to accelerate production, and continuously improving quality and performance through rapid iteration.

This role will also direct a team of local creatives to curate and elevate impactful, truly local content across both elements — such as graphics, photos, and videos — and templates spanning social media, presentations, websites, and print products. By fostering a culture of excellence and innovation, this role will play a vital part in achieving Canva’s mission of delivering a world-class, truly local design experience.

Specifically, this role will:

  • Operate with high ownership and autonomy while collaborating across multiple teams, functions, and time zones

  • Work at pace, balancing speed and quality, and adapting quickly to shifting priorities and evolving business needs

  • Leverage AI tools and workflows to scale content production and improve efficiency

  • Build and optimise repeatable systems for content creation, rather than one-off outputs

  • Maintain clear, proactive communication with stakeholders and drive alignment across teams

  • Lead creative reviews, retrospectives, and continuous improvement loops

  • Foster a high-performance team culture grounded in inclusion, psychological safety, and a bias for action

 

What you will do

Creative Direction

  • Develop a compelling creative vision that delivers and executes against the Country Content Strategy Lead and Country Manager’s strategic priorities.

  • Collaborate closely with local Marketing, SEO, and Community teams.

  • Translate country and regional strategies into locally relevant campaigns.

  • Drive AI adoption in production and content innovation, supporting new product formats and emerging trends to keep creative outputs fresh and competitive.

Content Creation & Curation

  • Oversee the creation of content, including design kits, campaign documents, creator briefs, and in-house production where needed.

  • Work with Freelance Copywriters and/or AI Copy to ensure copy is culturally relevant and adheres to our copy best practice standards.

  • Curate and editorially frame content for marketing initiatives, showcases, and seasonal calendars to elevate local relevance.

  • Proactively identify content gaps and curate assets that reflect strategic priorities and creative excellence.

  • Lead quality control of all content outputs, ensuring alignment with brand guidelines and maintaining high standards of visual and messaging quality.

Market Understanding & Cultural Insights

  • Build and maintain a deep knowledge of local culture, consumer behaviour, and design trends to inform content direction and strategy.

  • Conduct foundational content research, ensuring creative and editorial output aligns with strategic needs and cultural nuances.

  • Provide cultural expertise to scale content, ensuring authenticity and relevance to the local market across AICG, partnerships, and creators.

  • Champion hyperlocal design perspectives in collaboration with cross-functional teams.

  • Support building an editorial strategy for local content, ensuring Canva’s library reflects cultural relevance, diversity, and inclusive storytelling.

  • Advocate for the integration of global and underrepresented perspectives in content development and curation, upholding Canva’s commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

Content Performance Monitoring & Analysis

  • Conduct template and element audits to identify improvement areas and opportunities for new content.

  • Perform content performance and gap analysis, distilling insights into recommendations that guide future content creation and acquisition.

  • Leverage data, trends, and local insights to shape creative direction, enhance creator and in-house briefs, and inform design decisions.

  • Facilitate retrospectives and performance reviews to refine strategies and content effectiveness.

  • Actively raise discoverability challenges or product limitations that impact content visibility or engagement.

Partnership & Stakeholder Management

  • Partner closely with Country Content Strategy Lead, as well as collaborate with local SEO, Marketing, and Country Managers – to align on creative goals and content needs, and confidently prioritise and negotiate trade-offs.

  • Lead the rollout of local partnership content through culturally relevant creative strategies and campaigns.

  • Manage creative strategy, brand adherence, and feedback implementation to meet partner expectations and project goals.

  • Communicate initiatives and results to senior leadership, ensuring visibility across stakeholders.

Competitive Analysis

  • Monitor competitor activity and creative trends across the region to identify new opportunities and maintain strategic edge.

  • Use findings to inform the content roadmap and differentiate Canva's creative offerings in the local market.

Project Management

  • Monitor project execution, mitigate risks, and escalate challenges when necessary to ensure timely, high-quality outcomes.

  • Maintain visibility into campaign timelines and production volume goals across all creative operations.

  • Maintain an agile mindset and adapt quickly to shifting priorities and dynamic day-to-day needs.

Freelance & Creator Management

  • Oversee local freelance designers, managing recruitment, briefing, output review, and development.

  • Build strong relationships with the Creators Production and Community teams, providing hyperlocal direction through well-crafted briefs and feedback loops.

  • Champion Creator-led content that resonates deeply with local audiences and reflects cultural authenticity.

Reporting & Communication

  • Report on the performance and ROI of creative campaigns, using analytics to guide and improve future content plans and outputs.

  • Keep senior management and regional stakeholders informed about key initiatives, learnings, and creative progress.

  • Ensure alignment and transparency through consistent documentation and communication.

Feedback & Quality Assurance

  • Provide timely feedback and approvals across creative workstreams, maintaining alignment with both business goals and creative standards.

  • Drive internal reviews and uphold quality benchmarks for all deliverables across content types.

Team Building & Culture

  • Contribute to and foster a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing regional creative team culture.

  • Promote continuous improvement through process optimization, retrospectives, and shared best practices.

  • Encourage creative excellence while ensuring inclusion, psychological safety, and alignment across diverse teams.

 

What we're looking for

We’re looking for a high-performing design leader who combines strong creative craft with a builder mindset. You are culturally attuned, globally aware, and obsessed with creating content that feels truly local – and drives business results. You’ll be excited to join an A-player team committed to growing Canva in in your [locale].


You bring a sharp eye for design, but more importantly, you know how to deliver quality at speed. You operate with an AI-first mindset, using tools and systems to generate, iterate, and scale content efficiently – without compromising on craft.


You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and are comfortable working with evolving tools, shifting priorities, and imperfect information. You’re proactive, pragmatic, and outcome-focused—someone who takes ownership, moves quickly, and continuously looks for better ways of working.


You’re collaborative and low ego, able to partner effectively with Content Strategy, Marketing, SEO, and Product teams – translating strategic direction into content execution and driving alignment through clarity and action. You’re equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves to deliver work as you are guiding and uplifting others.

You’ll have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Design, Marketing, Communications, or a related field

  • Proven experience in creative leadership roles, ideally with international, regional, or market-level remit

  • A strong portfolio showcasing exceptional design work and content campaigns that reflect cultural resonance and local user needs

  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (SEO, Growth, Marketing, Product)

About the Group/Team

We're the Discovery group, part of Canva's Content & Discovery supergroup. Our mission is to enable every user to effortlessly find content that empowers them to design. Within the group, the Private Search Quality team owns helping users find their own personal, team, and branded content — the search experience people rely on every time they go looking for something they've already made or been given access to.

About the Role/Specialty

As a Machine Learning Engineer on Private Search Quality, you'll work on the ranking and relevance systems behind how Canva surfaces private, team, and brand content. That means building and improving ML ranking models and lifting relevance for all users, and helping the team's search results hold up as usage patterns and content types keep expanding, including newer surfaces like agent-driven search. It also means working with our Backend Engineers with our ElasticSearch and Vector Search databases. You'll take ownership of scoped projects end-to-end, from problem framing through to shipped, measurable impact on search quality.

There is a strong emphasis on experimentation and iterating on learnings to get the best outcomes for our users.

What you’ll do (responsibilities)

  • Build, evaluate, and improve ML ranking models for private, team, and brand content search

  • Drive relevance and recall improvements, with a particular focus on enterprise user outcomes

  • Work on intelligent result understanding, search recovery, and exact title match to help users navigate results

  • Contribute to indexing with a variety of technologies including ElasticSeach/OpenSearch, Vector search and annotation

  • Extend private and brand search quality and coverage into newer surfaces like agent search

  • Investigate and resolve quality or relevance regressions in production search

  • Communicate technical trade-offs clearly, including to non-technical stakeholders, and share knowledge across the team

What we're looking for:

You've got hands-on experience building and shipping ML systems in production, ideally in search, ranking, LTR or relevance, not just training models in a notebook. You're comfortable defining and moving the metrics that matter (relevance, recall, ranking quality) rather than just chasing model accuracy in isolation. You can take a scoped project from idea to shipped with minimal guidance, bringing your own judgement to how a problem should be solved rather than needing a fully defined solution handed to you. You're highly autonomous, comfortable with ambiguity as search surfaces and user needs evolve, and you want your work to show up in something real people use every day.


What You'll Learn & Build

  • Deep experience building and improving production ranking and relevance systems at Canva's scale

  • Exposure to how ML, product, and infra decisions intersect across the wider Discovery group

  • The chance to work on emerging surfaces like agent-driven search as the space develops

About the Role/Specialty

As a Senior Research Scientist on Design Generation, you'll work on the generative modelling problems behind how Canva creates and understands design content. That means training and evaluating design generation models at scale - from wrangling large-scale datasets, crafting training objectives that draw out the most from this data to improve design quality, evaluating them on criteria that users actually care about, and working with product teams to help ship those models to 250M+ users. You’ll take ownership of scoped research projects end-to-end, from framing an open problem through to a shipped or clearly validated result.

What you’ll do (responsibilities)

  • Train and evaluate generative models like LLMs for design generation

  • Design and run experiments to test hypotheses about model architecture, training approach, and data

  • Build and improve evaluation methods and benchmarks for measuring generative design quality

  • Translate research findings into techniques and approaches the team can move toward production

  • Investigate model quality issues, failure modes, and gaps against user and business needs

  • Stay current with generative modelling research and bring relevant advances into the team's work

  • Communicate research findings and trade-offs clearly, including to non-research stakeholders, and share knowledge across the team

What we're looking for:

You've got hands-on experience training generative models, ideally with exposure to image ordesigngeneration, not just applying pretrained models off the shelf. You're comfortable defining and moving the metrics that matter for generative quality, not just chasing benchmark numbers in isolation. You can take a scoped, often ambiguous research problem from framing to a validated result with minimal guidance, bringing your own judgement to how it should be approached. You're highly autonomous, comfortable with the ambiguity that comes with frontier research, and you want your work to show up in something real people use every day.

  • You've got hands-on, practical experience fine-tuning large language and multimodal models (LLMs/MLLMs) at scale in an industrial research setting.

  • You know the tricks of the trade: wrangling large-scale data pipelines, designing novel training objectives that extract the most from the data to improve design quality, and training and evaluating across multi-GPU setups

  • You've got a PhD in AI, machine learning, or a related field, plus at least two years of strong hands-on industry experience. We will also consider candidates without a PhD, but with at least 6 years of industry experience.

  • A background in diffusion or image generation is a bonus, not a requirement — the core need here is language and multimodal LLM depth


What You'll Learn & Build:

  • Deep experience researching and training generative models for design at Canva's scale

  • Exposure to how research, product, and infra decisions intersect across Canva Research and the wider Generative AI supergroup

  • The chance to work on frontier generative modelling problems as the space develops

We're the Discovery group, part of Canva's Content & Discovery supergroup. Our mission is to enable every user to effortlessly find content that empowers them to design. Within the group, the Private Search Quality team owns helping users find their own personal, team, and branded content — the search experience people rely on every time they go looking for something they've already made or been given access to.

About the Role/Specialty

As a Machine Learning Engineer on Private Search Quality, you'll work on the ranking and relevance systems behind how Canva surfaces private, team, and brand content. That means building and improving ML ranking models and lifting relevance for all users, and helping the team's search results hold up as usage patterns and content types keep expanding, including newer surfaces like agent-driven search. It also means working with our Backend Engineers with our ElasticSearch and Vector Search databases. You'll take ownership of scoped projects end-to-end, from problem framing through to shipped, measurable impact on search quality.

There is a strong emphasis on experimentation and iterating on learnings to get the best outcomes for our users.

What you’ll do (responsibilities)

  • Build, evaluate, and improve ML ranking models for private, team, and brand content search

  • Drive relevance and recall improvements, with a particular focus on enterprise user outcomes

  • Work on intelligent result understanding, search recovery, and exact title match to help users navigate results

  • Contribute to indexing with a variety of technologies including ElasticSeach/OpenSearch, Vector search and annotation

  • Extend private and brand search quality and coverage into newer surfaces like agent search

You can take a scoped project from idea to shipped with minimal guidance, bringing your own judgement to how a problem should be solved rather than needing a fully defined solution handed to you. You're highly autonomous, comfortable with ambiguity as search surfaces and user needs evolve, and you want your work to show up in something real people use every day.

  • Deep experience building and improving production ranking and relevance systems at Canva's scale

  • Exposure to how ML, product, and infra decisions intersect across the wider Discovery group

  • The chance to work on emerging surfaces like agent-driven search as the space develops

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hello, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

Our global HQ is in Sydney, Australia, and as we continue to grow in our largest global market, we’ve made our way from down under to San Francisco.

Our Jackson Square campus blends the neighborhood’s vibrant downtown charm with Canva’s signature flair. The space is designed for both deep work and collaboration, along with spaces for Canvanauts to relax, recharge, and connect. We offer flexibility in how and where you work. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

What you’d be doing in this role

Real Estate is Canva's largest vertical by revenue among our top accounts, and our Listings App is the reason enterprise real estate customers choose us. As we scale this vertical, we need someone to own the MLS onboarding experience end-to-end — coordinating across MLSs, brokerages, our data partner Constellation Data Labs, legal, finance, and engineering to get every customer live faster. That's where you come in.

As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavor of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

  • Own MLS onboarding end-to-end: Be the single point of accountability from the moment a deal closes — coordinating kickoff calls, tracking every active case, and keeping customers, MLSs, brokerages, and internal teams aligned through to go-live.

  • Navigate forms, agreements, and vendor registration: Complete MLS vendor questionnaires, prepare data license agreements and secure the necessary approvals, manage fee payments, and act as an authorized signer for Canva across MLS partnerships.

  • Build the playbook, then run it: Design and own a repeatable, documented onboarding process that scales with Canva's growth in this vertical.

  • Own compliance and audit: Review all active MLS connections for compliance gaps, manage renewals, and partner with finance and legal to keep every connection on solid ground.

  • Be the internal MLS expert: Advise Product on data requirements and roadmap decisions, flag compliance considerations, and help the team understand what great looks like for this space.

  • Drive automation and efficiency: Continuously look for ways to cut onboarding time and reduce manual steps in the process.

  • Manage and Grow Canva's PropTech Partner Ecosystem: Help identify and stand up new real estate data partnerships that deepen engagement and drive growth across the vertical. Including representing Canva at industry conferences and events.

You're probably a match if

We're looking for someone who knows the MLS world inside and out — with real relationships across the landscape, a sharp understanding of data licensing and compliance, and the process discipline to navigate a complex, multi-party ecosystem without dropping a ball.

  • Deep MLS expertise: 5+ years working directly with or within MLSs, real estate data providers, or real estate technology companies, with strong relationships across the industry.

  • Technical fluency: Solid knowledge of US MLS operations — IDX/VOW licensing, RESO standards, brokerage data release agreements, and the compliance requirements that come with them.

  • Legal and commercial comfort: You understand the legal considerations around MLS partnerships and are comfortable representing Canva as an authorized signer in negotiations and onboarding forms.

  • Process builder: You've built or run complex, multi-party workflows before (Airtable or similar tools are your friend), and you know how to bring order to ambiguity rather than waiting for someone else to write the playbook.

  • Communicator and translator: You can turn complex MLS requirements into clear, actionable briefs for legal, product, and engineering audiences, and represent Canva professionally in external negotiations.

  • Self-directed and detail-oriented: You prioritize a complex, high-stakes workload without being chased, and nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.

  • Industry Connections: you have deep industry connections with PropTech companies such as Cloze, Rechat, MoxiWorks, Lofty, Local Logic, and LiveBy.

  • API/MCP Fluency: You understand the basics of REST APIs, AppSDKs, and MCPs.

  • AI Power User: You use AI beyond the chatbot. You understand Claude Cowork or ChatGPT Work at the Agentic level. You build Skills and Scheduled Tasks to multiply your output.

  • Bonus: Experience with Constellation Data Labs, Cotality, or similar MLS data aggregators; familiarity with CREA or Canadian MLS systems; background in real estate law or data compliance.


About the team

As Real Estate Partnerships Manager, you'll be the single owner of MLS onboarding and Real Estate Tech Partners at Canva — the connective tissue between Sales, Legal, Product, our data partner Constellation Data Labs, MLSs, and our customers. You'll start by taking full ownership of every active MLS onboarding case, auditing existing connections, and building a documented, repeatable process from the ground up. From there, you'll expand your impact to existing/new real estate partnerships that help our customers get more value from Canva and drive growth across the vertical.

This is a role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, builds trust across a wide range of stakeholders, and takes real ownership of a process that today depends on no one in particular — and soon, will depend on you.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too

  • Health benefits plans to support you and your wellbeing

  • 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

At Canva we value fairness, and we strive to provide competitive, market-informed compensation whilst ensuring internal equity within the team in each region. We make hiring decisions based on your skills, experience and our overall assessment of what we observed and learnt in the hiring process. The target salary range for this position is $136,000 to $146,000 When calculating offers, we make salary decisions based on market data and candidates' skills and experience.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
About the role

Canva's generative models are judged by millions of people who will never read a benchmark. They just know whether the design looks right. Turning that judgement into something measurable is the hardest problem in our research stack, and it gates everything else. If we cannot measure design quality reliably, we cannot train against it, we cannot tell a real improvement from noise, and we cannot decide what ships.

We are looking for a Principal Research Scientist who defines what evaluation needs to become as the space gets harder, rather than running the playbook we already have. You will own how Canva evaluates generative quality across the whole of Canva Research, including problems we have not framed yet: new modalities, evaluation that reflects real differences between content types, user segments and markets, and a much tighter link between what our metrics say and what users and the business actually experience.

This is a Canva-wide craft leadership role, setting direction across our research groups in Australia, Europe, the US and China. You will be the person others come to when the numbers and the eyes disagree.

What you'll own

The evaluation strategy for Canva Research. Define what great evaluation looks like across design, image, video, audio and agentic workflows, and set the long-term direction for how Canva measures generative quality as the space evolves. You will shape the principles teams use to trade off evaluation compute, human data spend and signal fidelity, and you will defend them.

The science of measurement itself. Auto-raters and MLLM judges are only as good as their correlation with the thing they proxy for. You will treat that correlation as a research problem: validating metrics against human preference and downstream product outcomes, quantifying judge bias, and catching benchmark saturation and contamination before they quietly stop telling us anything.

The link between evaluation and what actually matters. Evaluation should reflect user experience and product impact, not just perform well in isolation. You own closing that gap, including the fact that a good evaluator is not automatically a good reward model for RL. That extends to the full experience rather than the artefact alone, editability included.

One standard across every region. Our teams in London, Vienna, San Francisco, Sydney and China all need to know they are measuring the same thing. You will build the shared evaluation layer that makes results comparable, and you will spot the collaboration opportunities nobody has been chartered to own yet. Taking that initiative is a core expectation of this role, not a bonus.

Focus areas

Human preference at scale. Rubric design, rater guidelines, inter-rater reliability, and calibration across markets and cultural contexts. Aesthetic judgement is not universal, and our evaluation systems need to hold that honestly rather than average it away.

Learned quality models and reward signals. Reward modelling and preference learning that feed post-training (RLHF, RLAIF) and inference-time selection, and being explicit about where a good judge does not translate into a good reward model.

Vision-Language Models for quality understanding. Novel architectures and training approaches for models that understand what makes a design effective, not just well-formed. These become the reward signal and feedback loop for our design generation models, so their failure modes are our failure modes.

Agentic and automated evaluation. MLLM-as-a-judge systems, model-based grading, and the infrastructure to run hundreds of evaluations against live training checkpoints without the results becoming noise.

Multimodal and segment-specific evaluation. Extending rigour into photo AI and video as they mature and start moving faster than traditional user research and marketing testing can cover, with evaluation that can be sliced meaningfully by doc type, user group and locale.

Evaluation in production. Offline evaluation suites and online monitoring, with regression detection that makes a quality drop impossible to miss before it reaches users.

External credibility. Benchmarking Canva's models against the frontier, and building evaluation work others in the industry look to. Publication and public reporting where it serves the mission.

We are looking for a Principal Research Scientist who defines what evaluation needs to become as the space gets harder, rather than running the playbook we already have. You will own how Canva evaluates generative quality across the whole of Canva Research, including problems we have not framed yet: new modalities, evaluation that reflects real differences between content types, user segments and markets, and a much tighter link between what our metrics say and what users and the business actually experience.

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Kamusta, hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Where and how you can work

Our flagship campus is in Sydney, Australia, but with many of our Canvanauts calling the Philippines home, our office in Manila is a buzzing place. Whether your role needs you in the office, at home or a bit of both, we've created an environment that truly empowers you to thrive.

What you’d be doing in this role

As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

Canva has a dedicated Internal Coaching Team, made up of professional coaches sitting inside the People function, as part of the People Experience Group.

This isn't a traditional executive coaching or L&D role. It's a specialist coaching function focused on mindset and behaviour change, not skills training and not performance management.

The purpose of the Internal Coaching team is to create radical mindset transformation, helping Canvanauts:

  • identify and overcome self sabotage and limiting beliefs
  • unlock strengths and potential
  • create lasting behavioural change

While coaching conversations may sometimes resemble psychology, the approach stays coaching-led: future-focused, action-focused, and built for meaningful change rather than long-term therapeutic support.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

1:1 Coaching

  • Structured 6-session coaching journeys, delivered fortnightly, one hour per session, over roughly 3 months.
  • Developmental, not directive. Coaches don't tell people what to do they help coachees shift the beliefs and patterns underneath their behaviour, not just the behaviour itself.'
  • Each coach typically carries 15 to 28 active coachees at a time, depending on their other program load.
  • Coaches also deliver Breakthrough Sessions: focused, single 60-minute sessions for someone working through one specific decision or pressure point.
  • Around 60% of each week is dedicated to 1:1 coaching.

Group Coaching

  • Coaches design and deliver group coaching programs such as a 3 month group coaching program focused on self-confidence and resilience, ran several times a year.
  • Contribute and facilitating Leadership Programs at Canva

Team coaching

  • Our Internal Coaches also facilitate team coaching requests. These are often 90min-2hr unblocking sessions, which are either once or or sometimes part of a longer team development journey.

Program contribution

  • Alongside direct coaching, the work includes

    • designing coaching experiences and resources
    • contributing specialist expertise
    • attending team meetings
    • participating in working groups

You're probably a match if you:

  • You bring a minimum of 5 years of dedicated professional 1:1 coaching experience, where coaching has been your primary role rather than one part of a broader HR, L&D, or people leadership position.
  • You have completed formal, recognised coach-specific training and accreditation, such as Meta-Coaching, Co-Active Coaching, Coach Masters Academy, Master Coaching Certification, Professional Coaching Certification, or another recognised transformational coaching methodology.
  • You have experience coaching individuals across different levels, rather than exclusively coaching senior leaders.
  • You bring deep transformational coaching capability and can explore root causes rather than focusing only on surface-level behaviours.
  • You have a strong understanding of transformational coaching methodologies.
  • You are available to work full-time, Mondays to Fridays, from 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM Philippine Time.

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
About the Group/Team

Canva's AI Platform Group provides the foundational infrastructure and tooling that powers AI features across the company, supporting MLEs, researchers, and AI builders from CORE and the wider organisation. Within the group, the Evaluation Platform team owns the end-to-end evaluation lifecycle: test-like evals integrated into developer workflows, the Arena comparative evaluation service, monitoring evals sampled from production traffic, and human labelling tooling. The team partners closely with AI feature teams, CORE researchers, and adjacent platform teams (Inference, Datasets, and Training) to make rigorous evaluation the default for every AI feature Canva ships.

About the Role/Specialty

We're seeking an engineering manager who can lead a large, senior team through a period of consolidation and growth. The Evaluation Platform team operates at the intersection of ML research practice and production platform engineering; you'll need enough technical depth in ML and evaluation to hold a credible strategic position, and the people leadership skills to coach a team of 9+ engineers, most of them senior. The role involves significant stakeholder complexity: multiple internal customer teams with competing priorities, adjacent teams with overlapping ambitions in the evaluation space, and a company-wide programme of work that runs through this team. You'll be expected to own and articulate the evaluation platform vision, not just execute a roadmap handed to you.

What you’ll do (responsibilities)

Coaching, mentoring, and growing a team that is a mix of specialties and skills while developing your coaching capability to scale the team and meet the needs of Canva's AI platform vision. You'll do this by:

  • Owning and evolving the evaluation platform strategy: consolidating test-like evals, comparative evaluation (Arena), monitoring evals, and labelling tooling into a coherent, self-serve platform.

  • Partnering with AI feature teams and CORE leadership to understand their roadmaps and proactively identify the evaluation capabilities needed for upcoming initiatives.

  • Coordinating with adjacent platform teams and the evals programme PM to ensure a seamless experience across the full ML lifecycle.

  • Owning and driving the delivery of large, cross-team, and cross-group initiatives from ideation to completion, with autonomy and independence of decision making.

  • Coaching a team of 9+ engineers by providing regular, practical feedback and collaboratively helping them reach their personal growth goals.

  • Owning the team's development methodology and rituals, such as planning cycles, stand-ups, and retrospectives.

  • Planning goals and defining success metrics to ensure alignment between the company, group, and team.

  • Championing a culture of knowledge sharing and advocating effectively for evaluation and ML engineering needs to stakeholders across Canva.

  • Running hiring and resourcing, including resourcing for the execution of the roadmap.

  • What we're looking for

  • A history of success in technical people leadership and mentorship of engineers, ideally including senior and staff-level ICs.

  • Experience with ML evaluation, LLM systems, or ML platform engineering; you understand what makes evaluating generative AI hard and can engage credibly with both researchers and engineers.

  • Experience designing and building complex, distributed systems, ideally involving machine learning.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills: comfortable navigating competing priorities across multiple customer teams and negotiating scope boundaries with adjacent teams.

  • First principles thinking; the ability to use deep understanding of a problem space to make informed decisions, even when those decisions differ from industry convention. Canva is a unique company solving unique problems, and this sometimes requires bold decisions.

  • A balance of strong technical and people leadership skills.

  • Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to break large projects into smaller ones and deliver on them through others.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Proven expertise in inspiring others to achieve their full potential and enabling the engineers in your team to do novel, impactful work.

  • A continuous learner attitude, energised by a problem space (GenAI evaluation) that is evolving month to month.
