jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Hey, g'day, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

What you'd be doing in this role:

Every native app Canva ships runs on a build and release system someone has to own, and right now that system sits on the critical path for the biggest client-side re-architecture in Canva's history. You'd be the engineer who takes that on: the Bazel rules, the monorepo, the release pipeline, the whole native foundation that hundreds of engineers build against every day.

Canva's mobile apps are moving off a browser-wrapped shell and onto a native-grade Portable Platform, and the build, release and CI foundations underneath that shift currently sit with a handful of people stitching together fragmented tooling. This role exists to give that foundation a single, deliberate owner, someone who can set the technical direction for iOS and Android build systems, the monorepo migration, and the React Native build pipeline that the Portable Platform depends on.

Bazel at mobile scale is still rare in this industry, which means most of the standards you'd set here don't exist yet anywhere else. You'd be defining what "good" looks like for build reliability, release safety and monorepo strategy across both platforms, and you'd be doing it with the benefit of a 12-month horizon rather than the current quarter, the difference between a senior engineer solving a defined problem and a staff engineer defining the problem worth solving.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Build architecture: own the roadmap for Bazel build rules, React Native bundling and codegen, making trade-offs between short-term fixes and long-term foundations.

  • Release infrastructure: mature Canva's mobile release and deployment tooling, including OTA and staged rollout, so shipping mobile is predictable rather than fragile.

  • Monorepo migration: lead the staged migration of mobile repos into Canva's monorepo, owning build, test and release continuity throughout.

  • CI/CD strategy: set the quality gating strategy across the build pipeline, surfacing reliability and speed problems before they're handed to you.

  • Cross-platform foundations: evolve the React Native build pipeline into a shared foundation that serves both web and mobile, not just mobile in isolation.

  • Stakeholder alignment: work across Mobile Workflows, Cross Platform, Build Platform and DevX to pull fragmented tooling into one coherent system.

  • Team leverage: build monitoring and health signals for builds and releases, and mentor engineers so the standards you set outlast any one project.

Success here looks like build and release infrastructure that other teams stop noticing because it just works, and a mobile monorepo strategy that product teams build against without having to think about the plumbing underneath it.

You’re probably a match:

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience:

  • Build systems: deep, hands-on expertise with Bazel, Gradle, or Xcode build systems at production scale.

  • Cross-team delivery: a track record of scoping and delivering complex projects that span multiple teams — migrations, monorepo consolidation, or build infrastructure at scale.

  • Mobile depth: strong native engineering background in iOS, Android, or both, with a real point of view on where cross-platform tooling helps and where it doesn't.

  • Release engineering: experience owning CI/CD or release pipelines that other teams depend on, not just contributing to them.

  • Strategic judgement: you balance short-term delivery against long-term architecture, and you can connect an external shift in tooling to a change in technical direction.

  • Standards setting: your documentation and technical practices have become the reference other engineers build on, not just something you wrote once.

Technical knowledge:

  • Bazel depth: build rules, custom rule sets, and monorepo build configuration at meaningful scale.

  • CI/CD pipelines: designing quality gates and pipeline stages that hold up as more teams depend on them.

  • React Native builds: bundling, codegen, and native module integration inside a production RN pipeline.

  • iOS build tooling: Xcode build system depth, including native iOS release configuration.

  • Android build tooling: Gradle depth, including native Android release configuration.

  • Release management: OTA updates, staged rollout, and deployment infrastructure for mobile apps.

  • Monorepo systems: experience migrating or operating within a large-scale monorepo.

Nice to have:

  • Cross-language interop: native bridging or codegen automation experience across JS and native runtimes.

  • Mobile performance: profiling and optimisation work on native or hybrid mobile apps.

  • Platform advocacy: experience getting engineering standards adopted beyond your own team.

  • Scale exposure: prior work on mobile products with a large, established user base.

About the Group and Team:

Join the Product Platform supergroup at Canva, where our mission is to build the pathways that empower Canva to deliver delightful experiences for billions of users.

Mobile Platform is the subgroup that provides optimal platform support for mobile development, from ideation to deployment, so that Canva's native apps feel delightful on every device. It sits within Product Platform alongside Client Platform, User Platform, API Platform and PIE, and currently spans the teams working on cross-platform product engineering and native mobile foundations.

Native Infra owns the native foundations underneath Canva's mobile apps: iOS and Android build systems, the migration of mobile repos into Canva's monorepo, release and deployment infrastructure, and the React Native build pipeline underpinning the Portable Platform. Every team shipping a mobile feature at Canva builds on top of what this team maintains, when Native Infra gets the foundation right, that reliability compounds across every product team that ships mobile.

What’s in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard — and we do — but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for success both in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages — we want our success to be yours too

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Other stuff to know?

We see AI as a powerful amplifier of creativity and technology at Canva. We're evolving how we assess AI skills in our Technology hiring experience — you'll tackle interactive, real-time challenges that reflect the kind of work we do. In some interviews, you may also be asked to solve a problem using an AI tool to show how you approach challenges with tech by your side.

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture.

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva, so even if you don't feel like your skills quite match what's listed above — we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

  • Build architecture: own the roadmap for Bazel build rules, React Native bundling and codegen, making trade-offs between short-term fixes and long-term foundations.

  • Release infrastructure: mature Canva's mobile release and deployment tooling, including OTA and staged rollout, so shipping mobile is predictable rather than fragile.

  • Monorepo migration: lead the staged migration of mobile repos into Canva's monorepo, owning build, test and release continuity throughout.

  • CI/CD strategy: set the quality gating strategy across the build pipeline, surfacing reliability and speed problems before they're handed to you.

  • Cross-platform foundations: evolve the React Native build pipeline into a shared foundation that serves both web and mobile, not just mobile in isolation.

  • Stakeholder alignment: work across Mobile Workflows, Cross Platform, Build Platform and DevX to pull fragmented tooling into one coherent system.

  • Team leverage: build monitoring and health signals for builds and releases, and mentor engineers so the standards you set outlast any one project.

Success here looks like build and release infrastructure that other teams stop noticing because it just works, and a mobile monorepo strategy that product teams build against without having to think about the plumbing underneath it.

You’re probably a match:

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience:

  • Build systems: deep, hands-on expertise with Bazel, Gradle, or Xcode build systems at production scale.

  • Cross-team delivery: a track record of scoping and delivering complex projects that span multiple teams — migrations, monorepo consolidation, or build infrastructure at scale.

  • Mobile depth: strong native engineering background in iOS, Android, or both, with a real point of view on where cross-platform tooling helps and where it doesn't.

  • Release engineering: experience owning CI/CD or release pipelines that other teams depend on, not just contributing to them.

  • Strategic judgement: you balance short-term delivery against long-term architecture, and you can connect an external shift in tooling to a change in technical direction.

  • Standards setting: your documentation and technical practices have become the reference other engineers build on, not just something you wrote once.

Technical knowledge:

  • Bazel depth: build rules, custom rule sets, and monorepo build configuration at meaningful scale.

  • CI/CD pipelines: designing quality gates and pipeline stages that hold up as more teams depend on them.

  • React Native builds: bundling, codegen, and native module integration inside a production RN pipeline.

  • iOS build tooling: Xcode build system depth, including native iOS release configuration.

  • Android build tooling: Gradle depth, including native Android release configuration.

  • Release management: OTA updates, staged rollout, and deployment infrastructure for mobile apps.

  • Monorepo systems: experience migrating or operating within a large-scale monorepo.

Nice to have:

  • Cross-language interop: native bridging or codegen automation experience across JS and native runtimes.

  • Mobile performance: profiling and optimisation work on native or hybrid mobile apps.

  • Platform advocacy: experience getting engineering standards adopted beyond your own team.

  • Scale exposure: prior work on mobile products with a large, established user base.

About the Group and Team:

Join the Product Platform supergroup at Canva, where our mission is to build the pathways that empower Canva to deliver delightful experiences for billions of users.

Mobile Platform is the subgroup that provides optimal platform support for mobile development, from ideation to deployment, so that Canva's native apps feel delightful on every device. It sits within Product Platform alongside Client Platform, User Platform, API Platform and PIE, and currently spans the teams working on cross-platform product engineering and native mobile foundations.

Native Infra owns the native foundations underneath Canva's mobile apps: iOS and Android build systems, the migration of mobile repos into Canva's monorepo, release and deployment infrastructure, and the React Native build pipeline underpinning the Portable Platform. Every team shipping a mobile feature at Canva builds on top of what this team maintains, when Native Infra gets the foundation right, that reliability compounds across every product team that ships mobile.

What’s in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard — and we do — but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for success both in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, こんにちは, 你好, hallo, नमस्ते, 안녕하세요, hola, salut!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job descriptions can feel a bit formulaic sometimes, but we promise Canva is anything but. If you're drawn to what we're building and you see yourself in this role, we'd love to hear from you.

Where and How You Can Work

This role is based in Vietnam. We believe in working where you do your best thinking — Canva offers flexibility to work in a way that suits you, whether that's remote, hybrid, or in-office.

What You'd Be Doing in This Role

Canva has over 250 million monthly active users across 190 countries, and Vietnam is one of our most exciting growth markets. We're building a local marketing team that's deeply rooted in the market, highly creative, and commercially sharp — and we need a Growth & Marketing Lead to sit at the centre of it all.

This is a well-rounded generalist role, not a performance specialist role. You'll own Vietnam's campaign calendar, shape the budget and channel strategy, lead partnerships, and make sure the whole team is pulling in the same direction. Our global search, ASO, and performance teams handle day-to-day media execution — your job is to own the strategic layer above that: setting priorities, guiding creative, and making sure Canva shows up consistently and effectively across every touchpoint in Vietnam.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Building and owning the Vietnam campaign calendar — aligning it with regional and global priorities, and coordinating the Social & Creative Lead, Design Lead, and Community Lead to bring multi-channel campaigns to life on time and on brief
  • Setting the media mix and leading budget allocation across channels, in close partnership with the Global Growth Marketing team
  • Guiding creative strategy using performance data — shaping briefs, and knowing when to scale, pause, or refresh
  • Building a strong working understanding of how performance marketing drives MAU and revenue in Vietnam, and using that to guide where we invest
  • Understanding the media measurement toolkit — MMM, incrementality studies, MMP and platform data — well enough to translate it into clear direction for the team
  • Contributing to Vietnam's partnership strategy: identifying the right partners, supporting negotiations, and building a framework the team can use to evaluate and prioritise opportunities

You're Probably a Match If:

  • You have well-rounded marketing experience across branding and multi-channel campaign management — you're as comfortable with a campaign brief as you are with a media plan
  • You've built and run campaign calendars before, coordinating multiple stakeholders to land them on time
  • You have a strong understanding of media buying principles and the modern measurement toolkit (MMM, lift studies, incrementality testing) — enough to guide strategy and budget decisions, even if you're not running campaigns day-to-day
  • You've developed partnership strategy and negotiated directly with partners, from first conversation to signed agreement
  • You're a strong cross-functional operator — you know how to coordinate without direct authority and keep diverse teams aligned toward a shared outcome
  • You're comfortable in a fast-paced, remote, multi-market environment and you make things happen without waiting for perfect conditions

About the Team

Vietnam's marketing team blends creativity, partnerships, and data to make Canva show up at its best in the market. You'll work closely with the Social & Creative Lead, Design Lead, and Community Lead locally, and connect into the broader regional and global marketing organisation. It's a collaborative, high-trust team with real ambition — and this role sits at the centre of it.

What's in It for You?

Canva has grown hugely over the last few years, but we're only just getting started. Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job ads can feel a bit formulaic sometimes, but we promise Canva is anything but. If you're drawn to what we're building and you see yourself in this role, we'd love to hear from you.

Where and How You Can Work

Our London office is a hub for collaboration and energy. But we also believe in working where you do your best thinking. This role is based in London, with the flexibility to work in a way that suits you.

Canva's mission is to empower the world to design. With 285+ million monthly active users across 190+ countries, we're building the world's most loved visual communication platform. We're not a template tool. We're an AI-powered visual work platform that's replacing legacy tools across design, documents, presentations, video, and websites.

About the role: 

  • This is not an operations role, and it is not a "run the playbook" role. We're looking for a strategist who will figure out what the playbook should be.
  • You'll sit on the International Supergroup Leadership Team (SGL) and work directly with the Head of International to answer two questions. Top-down: how should we segment our markets and allocate investment across them? Bottom-up: what causally drives growth in each market, and how do we make it repeatable? International is accountable for both MAU and ARR.
  • In this role you'll form hypotheses, follow hunches, place bold bets, and validate with data. You'll partner closely with the Data Lead, Finance Lead, Leadership Operations, Country Managers, and central product, content and marketing teams. The team is globally distributed: leadership across Sydney, Europe and Dubai time zones, specialties in Sydney, and teams in every market, which gives this role real autonomy.


What you'll do:
Portfolio Strategy (Top-Down):

  • Segment the 23 Pioneer markets by penetration, maturity and competitive landscape, and decide how our playbook should differ: one playbook with modules maximised per market, or different playbooks for different clusters.
  • Shape investment allocation. Partner with Finance to build the principles for deploying headcount, contingent workers and marketing budget across the portfolio, and feed the monthly MBR conversation.
  • Pressure-test market and vertical bets. Invest more in some countries to grow them faster while doing product-only work in others. Build the cases and make the calls with the Head of International.

Growth Drivers & Funnel Excellence (Bottom-Up)

  • Find the causal growth drivers. Go beyond correlation to identify what genuinely drives each stage of the funnel in each market, across product-led growth and product distribution, working hand in hand with the International Data Lead.
  • Diagnose and tighten the funnel. Analyse why the same product produces 20% 7-day activation in one market and 35% in another, isolate the causes (content, localisation, payments, channels), and turn them into prescriptive plays countries can run.
  • Crystallise what you find into repeatable playbooks. You don't have to write every playbook, but you identify the causalities so they become repeatable by the countries.

Scaling What Works Across Markets

  • Work with Country Managers and develop growth hunches with them, validate what's working locally, and make it scalable. Retention and reactivation playbooks for markets like Brazil are the first proving ground.
  • Live in exploration mode. Form hypotheses, follow hunches, place bold bets, and validate with data. Win buy-in from stakeholders through evidence rather than authority.


You're a match if you have:

  • Exceptional analytical skills. You structure ambiguous problems, separate causality from correlation, and draw conclusions others miss.
  • Proven growth strategy experience at a consumer technology or digital platform company, with results you can personally attribute. You can articulate a clean growth thesis backed by data, not just intuition.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. You are energised by open questions, form a hunch, pursue it, and course-correct fast.
  • Genuine growth instinct. You understand funnels end to end, from acquisition and activation through to monetisation and retention, and you bring strong user intuition to match the data.
  • Strategic range. You can zoom out to portfolio-level allocation questions and zoom in to why one market's activation rate breaks.
  • Data-led decision maker with a strong experimentation mindset. You don't rely on gut alone: you test, measure, and iterate.
  • Bold, with bias to action. You place bets, hustle to validate them, and would rather be proven wrong fast than right slowly.
  • Exceptional stakeholder craft. You align Country Managers, Finance and central teams behind your recommendations, and you're comfortable operating in a matrix organisation with distributed authority.
  • Intellectually honest and first-principles driven. You say what the data says, flag problems early, deconstruct problems from the ground up rather than copy-pasting playbooks, and can articulate why a strategy should work in a specific market.


Highly valued:

  • Experience across international or multi-market environments, where the same product behaves differently by market.
  • Depth in monetisation and conversion (pricing, payments, upgrade flows), given the ARR side of the mandate.
  • Hands-on experience with causal inference and experiment design.
  • Genuine familiarity with Canva as a product. We expect you to have used it, not just researched it for the interview.

Canva is a force for good. We believe in empowering everyone to design. We're building a company where the best people want to do their best work. If you're the kind of strategist who gets energised by open questions and wants your analysis to move real markets, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Group/Team

Join Client Platform at Canva, where our mission is to ensure a delightful experience for every user on every device. Client Platform owns the foundations that every product team builds on, including Web Platform, Mobile Platform, and the user-facing surfaces of the product. Hundreds of millions of users sit on top of what this group ships. Every Canva product runs on it.

Mobile Platform is the group inside Client Platform responsible for how Canva runs on iOS and Android. We're the team for engineers who care deeply about mobile performance, who want to shape how cross-platform mobile gets built at scale, and who want to own the next decade of how Canva runs on a phone or tablet.

The work compounds in two directions at once. Every team at Canva benefits when the mobile platform gets faster and more capable. And the architectural decisions made here will outlast most of the systems built on top of them.

It's early: the team's small today (five Staff engineers and one Principal) and growing fast, and a lot of the wider org is upskilling into React Native from other specialties to get there. That means real room to shape how the team works, not just execute an existing playbook.

What you'd be doing in this role:

Canva's mobile app is built on web technology today. We're moving to a hybrid stack instead: React Native and React DOM working side by side, so we get one shared codebase across iOS, Android and web, without giving up native-grade performance. The parts that genuinely need speed — video, rendering, streaming — run in Rust and C++.

This role is the team's React Native expert. You'll help engineers who've only ever built for the browser make the shift to thinking in React Native: knowing exactly where "it's just React, it'll mostly work" stops being true, when to drop into a native implementation instead, and how to make React Native hold up at real product scale.

It's a flexible role and still early days for the team, so what you focus on first will depend on what's needed most when you join — likely a mix of platform tooling, performance work, and building the wider team's React Native fluency.

You're probably a match:


We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better, and we're invested in helping you grow into the rest.

Experience

  • React Native at real scale: you've worked with React Native inside a large company, on a product with genuine technical and product complexity

  • Performance under pressure: you've hit and solved real React Native performance problems

  • Credible technical expertise and leadership you can talk honestly about where React Native falls short, and you've convinced skeptics through weighing trade-offs and overcoming technical limitations

  • Cross-team influence: you've changed how more than one team builds, through documentation, tooling or direct collaboration.

  • Hands-on, recently: writing code day to day, with recent commits, design docs and reviews.

  • AI fluency: you've used AI tooling in real engineering work and have a view on what it changes for frontend or mobile development.

Nice to have:

  • Experience leading or influencing an organisation with a lot of contributors.

  • Comfort with the trade-offs of Rust or C++ in a mobile performance context.

  • Open-source contributions to React Native or the wider React ecosystem.

  • Design system or component library depth.

About the Group/Team
Canva’s mission is to empower the world to design. With over 220 million users already on board, we have a bold vision to reach 1 billion users. The CJKI Group is dedicated to this mission, pouring our hearts and souls into driving hyperlocalization. We strive to make Canva feel like a local experience in China, Japan, South Korea, and India, ensuring that our platform resonates deeply with users in these regions.


About the Role/Specialty
This role is for a high-performance, highly efficient Product Manager who thrives without a fixed lane — focusing on high-impact, high-ambiguity initiatives across Canva's core growth entry points and platform-level experiences, and moving across domains and markets as business priorities requires. You will operate in a highly complex organizational environment, driving alignment, making clear trade-offs, and delivering measurable outcomes quickly, in unfamiliar territory, with minimal ramp-up time 

What you’ll do (responsibilities)

Big Bets Project Owner (CJKI Scope)

  • Own end-to-end product strategy, execution, and outcomes for major initiatives
  • Translate global product vision into actionable, market-appropriate solutions for CJKI
  • Define MBR metrics (input, output & guardrails) and continuously track impact

Product Strategy & Decision-Making

  • Rapidly build deep understanding of user behavior and pain points in whatever domain or market you’re deployed to
  • Make high-quality decisions under uncertainty, even with incomplete data or insights
  • Balance global consistency vs. regional differentiation, clearly articulating trade-offs

Cross-functional Collaboration & Influence

  • Partner closely with Growth, Subscription, Homepage, Brand, Design, Infra, Data, Marketing, and other teams
  • Quickly building credibility with new partners each time you move onto a new initiative
  • Drive alignment and execution without direct reporting authority
  • Communicate progress, risks, and key decisions clearly to senior stakeholders, including Big Bets leaders

Experimentation & Iteration

  • Reduce uncertainty through A/B testing, phased rollouts, and experimentation frameworks — grounding every experiment in a clearly articulated intent and hypothesis, with input metrics, outcome metrics, and guardrails defined upfront rather than after the fact.
  • Learn quickly, iterate rapidly, and strike the right balance between speed and quality, treating every result — positive or negative — as a source of durable learning rather than a simple ship/no-ship verdict

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
What we're looking for

Must-have

  • 5–8+ years of Product Management experience, with ownership of high-impact, cross-functional initiatives
  • Strong experience in Growth or Monetization, with a demonstrated track record of being able to move across multiple product domains rather than staying only in a single lane — you're energized by picking up new problem spaces quickly, not just going deep in one.
  • Strong structured thinking: breaks down ambiguous problems with rigor, reasons through edge cases and second-order effects before committing to a direction, rather than jumping straight to a solution
  • Clear communicator and documenter: translates that thinking into thorough PRDs, tailors messages to the audience, and stays organized — tracking work in Jira and keeping stakeholders proactively updated
  • Strong data fluency, able to combine data and user insights to drive decisions
  • Deep understanding of at least one CJKI market (China / Japan / Korea/ India), with the ability to scale insights beyond a single market
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders you haven’t worked with before
  • Actively uses AI to amplify their own output and impact — from speeding up research to prototyping and finding new ways AI can extend what one PM can cover across multiple initiatives — rather than treating AI as optional or someone else's job
  • Fluent in English and comfortable working in a global context

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with product growth, ecommerce, or subscription domain
  • Proven success handling regional differentiation and localization in global products
  • Background in B2C or Product-Led Growth (PLG) environments

Today, much of Canva’s mobile product runs as a web application inside a native app shell. We’re moving towards a hybrid architecture built around React and React Native, supported by native iOS and Android capabilities, portable libraries and shared mobile infrastructure.

The ambition is simple to describe and difficult to execute: build once, ship native-feeling experiences across iOS, Android and web.

React Native is the direction we’re taking, but this role is bigger than expertise in a single framework. We’re also interested in Principal-level engineers who have solved comparable problems through Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform or other production-scale cross-platform architectures, and are excited to transfer that expertise into what we’re building.

This is a genuinely rare problem: evolving a mature mobile architecture while the product remains live for hundreds of millions of users and hundreds of engineers continue building on top of it. The decisions made here will shape how Canva builds mobile for the next decade.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Set the technical direction: Own the key architectural decisions for Canva’s hybrid mobile platform across React Native, iOS and Android, including what should be shared, what should remain native, and how those layers work together.

  • Get the new platform into production: In your first few months, you’ll turn the architecture into shipped code, with the foundations for performance, reliability and observability in place.

  • Prove it on a real product surface: Within six months, the goal is to have a React Native surface live in production, supported by stable capabilities and platform primitives that feature teams can build on.

  • Lead senior engineers through the migration: Be the architectural anchor for Staff and Senior engineers across Mobile Platform, helping them navigate difficult technical decisions as the new platform takes shape.

  • Scale adoption across Canva: In the new year, work with major product teams moving onto the platform, establishing patterns engineers trust and choose to use. Over time, you’ll become one of Canva’s technical voices on mobile architecture, with decisions influencing 800+ frontend engineers.

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

React Native and React are highly relevant, but deep experience with Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform or another production-scale cross-platform stack can also be compelling.

  • Migration at scale: Led a meaningful migration of a mature mobile product onto a new architecture while it remained live and growing. The stronger signal is changing an existing system at scale, rather than starting clean.

  • Principal-level technical leadership: Set technical direction across multiple teams where the answer wasn’t obvious, brought senior engineers and leaders with you, and had Staff-level engineers building against the direction you established.

  • Organisation-wide influence: You’ve shaped architecture beyond your immediate team, creating platforms, standards or technical direction adopted across multiple groups or a large engineering organisation.

  • Hands-on technical depth: You’re still close to the code and comfortable working through hard implementation details, not just setting direction from a distance.

  • Engineering judgement: You don’t need to arrive as a React Native evangelist. You do need to reason from first principles, challenge assumptions constructively and help make Canva’s chosen architecture successful at scale.

Technical knowledge

  • Mobile runtime: Shared-code runtimes, native boundaries, bundle delivery and performance profiling on real devices

  • iOS and Android: Deep fundamentals across both platforms and a strong instinct for where shared abstractions stop making sense

  • Mobile performance: Performance, reliability, crash monitoring and optimisation at scale

  • Platform architecture: Shared capabilities, libraries, abstractions and infrastructure used across multiple engineering teams

  • Deep fundamentals: Strong engineering fundamentals, including data structures, complexity and system-level trade-offs

Nice to have

  • React Native at scale: Deep production experience with React Native and React internals

  • System languages: Rust or C/C++ for portable libraries that run across mobile platforms

  • Open-source contributions: React Native, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform, Expo or the wider cross-platform mobile ecosystem

  • Mobile CI/CD: Release trains and over-the-air updates at scale

  • AI fluency: You’ve used AI tooling in real engineering work and have a view on how it changes the way mobile teams build and operate software.

About the team

You'll be joining our Client Platform group at Canva, where our mission is to ensure a delightful experience for every user on every device. Client Platform owns the foundations that every product team builds on, including Web Platform, Mobile Platform, and the user-facing surfaces of the product. The work compounds in two directions at once. Every team at Canva benefits when the mobile platform gets faster and more capable. And the architectural decisions made here will outlast most of the systems built on top of them.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design

Hey, g'day, ciao, buongiorno, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Where and how you can work

While we support flexible ways of working, our preference for this role would be in Milan, working in a hybrid capacity. You'll have the flexibility to balance remote focused work with in-person collaboration, while partnering with team members in Italy and Canva's global SEO community. We have a co-working space in Wellio Milano Dante.

This is a full-time contingent worker opportunity for 12 months with the opportunity to extend.

About the team

You'll join the Logged Out Experience Group within Canva's Growth Supergroup, working with teams focused on growing Canva's reach and helping more people discover what they can create.

You'll work in a locally embedded model while connecting into Canva's broader SEO community. That means partnering closely with stakeholders in Italy while collaborating with SEO specialists, product managers, content specialists and other experts globally.

The opportunity is bigger than growing SEO in one country. What you learn in Italy can help shape frameworks, systems and approaches that support Canva's growth across international markets.

What you'd be doing in this role

As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

International growth is a major focus for Canva. We're moving beyond translating strategies that have worked elsewhere and building truly local approaches that reflect how people discover and use Canva in individual markets.

As our SEO Country Lead for Italy, you'll lead Canva's SEO growth in the Italian market. You'll define and execute an SEO strategy grounded in local search behaviour, user needs and market opportunities, while connecting your work to Canva's broader growth priorities.

You'll own the strategy across technical SEO, content and authority building. You'll be both a strategist and an operator: identifying opportunities, prioritising what matters, influencing stakeholders and turning insights into measurable growth.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Owning the end-to-end SEO strategy for Italy across technical SEO, content and authority building, creating a focused roadmap aligned with Canva's international growth goals.
  • Becoming a trusted expert on Italy's search landscape by analysing user intent, search behaviour, competitors and emerging market trends.
  • Identifying and prioritising high-impact opportunities that grow organic sessions, signups, active users, returning users and overall search visibility.
  • Partnering with localisation, design, product, engineering, data and content teams to create high-quality experiences that feel genuinely relevant to people in Italy.
  • Maintaining strong technical SEO foundations across areas including site speed, crawlability, indexation, structured data, hreflang and mobile optimisation.
  • Building effective ways of working, reporting frameworks and repeatable processes that enable the market to operate with increasing autonomy.
  • Exploring how search and discovery are evolving through AI-powered experiences, including AI search, GEO and AEO, and sharing learnings that can help Canva grow globally.

You're probably a match if

  • You're a native Italian speaker with business-level English, with a deep understanding of Italian search behaviour, cultural nuances and internet user dynamics.
  • You've successfully led SEO initiatives for large websites and understand how technical SEO, content and authority building work together.
  • You're comfortable developing a market strategy from the ground up — using data and local knowledge to decide where to invest rather than simply following an existing global playbook.
  • You're highly analytical and can turn performance data into clear priorities, KPIs and recommendations that connect SEO activity to business impact.
  • You're a strong relationship builder who can influence without authority, work across disciplines and communicate complex SEO topics clearly to different audiences.
  • You bring an ownership mindset: you're comfortable with autonomy, proactively solve problems and find ways forward when resources, processes or dependencies create blockers.
  • You're curious about how discoverability is changing and are already thinking beyond traditional search engines to AI-powered search, LLMs, social search and emerging channels.
  • You're comfortable working with SEO and analytics tools such as Looker, Omni, Search Console, SEMrush, Ahrefs, Screaming Frog and similar platforms.
  • Experience developing multi-year market expansion strategies, working in hyper-growth environments, mobile-first optimisation or multi-platform search ecosystems would be a bonus.

What's in it for you?

This is an opportunity to take meaningful ownership of SEO for one of Canva's international markets. You'll develop your ability to build locally relevant growth strategies while operating within a global organisation, strengthen your cross-functional influence and contribute insights that can shape how Canva approaches international SEO.

You'll also have the opportunity to explore the changing future of search and discoverability — experimenting with new approaches and helping build the methodologies Canva can use as user behaviour evolves.

Other stuff to know

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture. When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process.

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva, so even if you don't feel like your skills quite match everything listed above, we still want to hear from you.

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually. Please submit your CV & application in English.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
At Canva, our mission is to empower the world to design. We’re building AI that feels magical and lands real impact for millions of people - helping anyone create with confidence. We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to own the data foundations that power our multimodal agent research—building the pipelines, datasets, and tooling that turn ambitious research ideas into trainable reality.

About the team

We explore multimodal agentic architectures, build scalable training and evaluation loops, and partner closely with product and platform teams to turn breakthroughs into delightful product features. We are a cutting-edge research team, developing new multimodal agentic systems. We work on all topics of multimodal modelling, pre/post-training and design agents, we build scalable training and evaluation loops, and partner closely with product and platform teams to turn breakthroughs into delightful product features.

About the role

You'll be responsible for the data lifecycle that fuels our agent research: from collection and curation through to preprocessing, quality assurance, and delivery into training pipelines. You'll work closely with research scientists to understand what data is needed, then design and build the systems to make it happen—reliably and at scale. You'll have significant autonomy over how data problems get solved, while aligning on what problems matter most with the broader team.

What you'll do

  • Design and build data pipelines for agent training: collection, filtering, deduplication, formatting, and versioning across text, image, and multimodal sources.

  • Build and maintain infrastructure for efficient data loading, storage, and retrieval at scale (S3, distributed systems, streaming pipelines).

  • Collaborate with research scientists to translate research requirements into concrete data specifications, and iterate as experiments reveal new needs.

  • Create evaluation datasets and benchmarks in collaboration with researchers—curating task distributions that surface real failure modes.

  • Develop tooling for dataset construction—including human annotation workflows, synthetic data generation, and preference data collection for RLHF/DPO-style training.

  • Own data quality: build validation frameworks, monitor for drift and contamination, and establish standards that make datasets trustworthy and reproducible.

  • Document datasets thoroughly: provenance, known limitations, intended use cases, and versioning history.

  • Implement comprehensive test coverage for data pipelines and ML workflows, ensuring reliability and catching regressions early.

  • Elevate codebase quality through code reviews, refactoring, and establishing engineering best practices that help research velocity scale sustainably.

  • Contribute to team roadmaps by identifying data bottlenecks and proposing solutions that unblock research velocity.

You're likely a match if you have

  • Strong software engineering skills in Python, with experience building production-grade data pipelines and ML DevOps.

  • Practical experience with prompt engineering—designing, testing, and refining prompts for reliable LLM/VLM outputs.

  • Experience with ML data workflows: large-scale data processing and loading (Ray, or similar), data versioning, and format considerations for training (tokenization, batching, sharding).

  • Hands-on experience working with data pipelines for large-scale distributed ML training runs.

  • Familiarity with annotation tooling and human-in-the-loop data collection (Label Studio or internal systems).

  • Understanding of ML training requirements—you know what "good data" looks like for LLM/VLM fine-tuning and can anticipate downstream issues.

  • Experience loading and writing large datasets to/from cloud infrastructure (AWS) and distributed storage systems.

  • Strong communication skills: you can work with researchers to scope ambiguous problems and translate needs into actionable plans.

  • A collaborative approach, comfortable taking ownership and iterating quickly.

Nice to have

  • Experience with preference data collection for RLHF or reward modelling.

  • Familiarity with multimodal data (image-text pairs, video, design assets).

  • Experience building synthetic data generation pipelines using LLMs.

  • Background in data quality metrics and monitoring systems.

  • Contributions to dataset releases or benchmarks in the ML community.

jobDescription.text:

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time-consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

Our hybrid way of working gives you the flexibility to work remotely and to come together on campus for meaningful in-person collaboration and connection when it matters most. We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.


What you'd be doing in this role

As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

Performance is fundamental to Canva's editing experience. As we grow, our editor needs to remain fast, smooth and reliable across different devices, networks and increasingly complex designs.

The Editing Performance team is rebuilding foundational parts of Canva's editor architecture, primarily in TypeScript with a growing amount of React Native and native development. You'll have the opportunity to work deep in the foundations of the editor, helping it perform at scale while making it easier for engineering teams across Canva to build performant experiences.

At the moment, this role is focused on:

  • Designing, developing and deploying software solutions, partnering closely with engineering leads, designers and product managers to deliver experiences for Canva's global community.

  • Working primarily in TypeScript as we rebuild core parts of the editor, with opportunities to work across React Native and native surfaces.

  • Driving measurable performance improvements across the editor, using performance data and instrumentation to understand problems, prioritise opportunities and demonstrate impact.

  • Building tools, frameworks and libraries that empower other engineers at Canva to create performant features.

  • Taking ownership of complex technical problems, breaking larger initiatives into achievable pieces and driving work from idea through to delivery.

  • Sharing technical knowledge and identifying opportunities to collaborate across teams on improvements that help us achieve our goals.

You're probably a match if

  • You have strong commercial software engineering experience and have worked on complex, large-scale applications, SDKs or APIs.

  • You have deep TypeScript experience and are comfortable navigating large, long-lived codebases, including reasoning about systems and types you didn't originally build.

  • You've contributed to architecture decisions and enjoy solving complex engineering problems rather than simply building within established patterns.

  • You're comfortable working with performance data — instrumenting metrics, interpreting dashboards and using evidence to prioritise work and demonstrate impact.

  • You bring strong computer science and engineering fundamentals, including asynchronous programming, data structures, solution design, architecture and design patterns.

  • You're curious about how software performs under the hood. Experience with browser rendering, event handling, WebWorkers or WebGL/WebGPU is a strong plus, while familiarity with native rendering pipelines or JavaScript engine internals is a bonus.

  • You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively and enjoy sharing knowledge while helping others solve difficult technical problems.

About the team

The Editing Group builds the core design experience at the heart of Canva. We work across the systems that make editing intuitive, responsive and scalable, tackling challenges spanning rendering performance, interactive design experiences and seamless cross-platform editing.

Within Editing, the Editing Performance team focuses on making sure performance never gets in the way of creativity. We improve page load and interaction performance, tackle memory and reliability challenges, build the measurement systems that help teams understand performance, and create frameworks that empower engineers across Canva to make performance part of how they build.

Our ambition is simple but challenging: Canva's editor should perform brilliantly regardless of platform, device, network or design complexity.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard — and we do — but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers

  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and support you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

We trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.

About the team structure

Our Operations Partnering Speciality is dispersed throughout Canva, supporting our different functions to deliver on their big goals. This Speciality runs as a triad: a Chief of Staff (called Leadership Operations at Canva), who holds executive-layer context, an Operations Business Partner, who owns the Supergroup's broader cadences, priorities and initiatives, and an Admin Business Partner (that’s you!) who unlocks Lead capacity through exceptional 1:1 executive support. Both the Operations Business Partners and the Admin Business Partner report to the Leadership Operations, who then reports to the executive.

About the role

As Admin Business Partner (Executive Assistant) you'll design and own the operating system that helps your executive lead effectively. Managing their calendar, inbox, travel, and the judgement calls that come with protecting their time are all part of the key focus: making sure the right things get their attention and focus at the right moment.

This has real scope beyond traditional executive support. You'll be trusted to make calls independently, spot what needs attention before being asked, and help shape how the the exec and their leadership team operate, rather than just keeping things ticking along.

What you'll be doing

Own the Lead's day-to-day operations

  • Run a calendar and inbox that's constantly shifting, exercising real judgement on what needs the Lead's attention now, what can wait, and what shouldn't land on their desk at all

  • Navigate a dense web of relationships across other senior leaders' support teams, where protocol and discretion matter as much as logistics

  • Plan and run the exec's travel, expenses and personal logistics end to end, so all of it is taken care of in the background

Keep the leadership rhythm running

  • Own the prep behind your exec’s leadership team's meeting cadence, translating what's happening across the org into what the exec and their Leads need to walk in ready in partnership with Leadership Operations

  • Play a critical role in the operational drumbeat of the org, helping to coordinate major moments such as global events, offsites and key launches

  • Build and maintain scalable workflows for recurring processes (e.g. approvals, planning rhythms, tracking mechanisms)

  • Continuously identify friction points, diagnose root causes and redesign underlying processes to improve how the org operates

  • Coordinate across stakeholders to ensure timelines, milestones and deliverables stay on track

Support the wider team and its culture

  • Make recognition part of the rhythm, not an afterthought: running things so achievements, milestones and departures actually get seen

  • Plan moments that bring the team together, like Force for Good (charity) days and other get-togethers

  • Handle the personal touches that make people feel looked after: organising gifts, writing notes, and marking what matters to them

  • Handle sensitive or fast-moving people matters with real discretion, given that almost everything crossing this desk is high-stakes and complex

You'll probably be a match if

  • You have 5+ years' experience partnering 1:1 with a senior leader, and can point to specific examples of protecting their time or capacity at real scale

  • You've owned a defined project or process end-to-end, not just supported one

  • You're genuinely comfortable holding a lot of moving pieces at once, and can prioritise under pressure without dropping the details that matter

  • You build trust quickly across a wide network, from senior leaders down to other ABPs and Ops partners, and know when to lean on that network rather than solving everything on your own

  • You're happy operating with real autonomy, including making judgment calls before checking in, when the situation calls for it

  • You're keen to take on the small stuff just as readily as the big visible wins, and jump in to help a teammate whenever it's needed

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

About the Role
As our Korean Language Manager, you’ll be responsible for making Canva feel truly local for users in Korea.

You’ll shape how Canva sounds and feels across Product, Marketing, Content, and other key surfaces, making sure the Korean experience is clear, natural, culturally relevant, and consistent.

This is much more than a translation role. You’ll be the language and cultural expert for Korea, working closely with Product, Design, Engineering, Marketing, and Localisation teams to identify opportunities, improve quality, and advocate for Korean users across Canva.

You’ll also help us evolve how we work as localisation becomes increasingly AI-enabled, balancing quality, scale, automation, and the moments where human craft matters most.
 

What you’ll do (responsibilities)

  • Shape Canva’s voice across Product, Marketing, Content, and other user-facing experiences in Korean.

  • Translate, review, transcreate, and adapt key content when needed.

  • Own and evolve Korean linguistic assets, including style guides, glossaries, and terminology.

  • Regularly audit Canva’s Korean experience and proactively identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Review vendor translations and provide actionable quality feedback.

  • Work with localisation partners to improve quality and consistency over time.

  • Provide cultural and linguistic guidance to teams across Canva.

  • Support product testing and localisation QA for new features and launches.

  • Use user insights, quality data, and product signals to prioritise localisation opportunities.

  • Experiment with AI-assisted localisation workflows and help evaluate their quality for Korean.

  • Help us decide where automation can scale and where human expertise remains essential.

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
What we're looking for
You’re a strong Korean writer with excellent linguistic judgement and a deep understanding of how language, culture, and context shape the way people experience a product.

You know that great localisation goes beyond translating words. You think about the full user experience, including tone, messaging, terminology, visual context, and whether something genuinely feels right for Korean users.

You’re proactive and comfortable working in ambiguity. You don’t wait for issues to be reported, you explore the product, identify opportunities, and work with others to improve them.

You’re also comfortable influencing people who don’t report to you. You can explain linguistic and cultural recommendations clearly to non-linguistic stakeholders and use context, user insights, data, or examples to bring others along.

 

You’ll ideally bring:

  • Native Korean language proficiency and excellent writing skills.

  • Professional-level English communication skills.

  • Experience in localisation, language management, UX writing, content design, translation, transcreation, or a related field.

  • Experience maintaining linguistic quality across multiple content types and surfaces.

  • Strong understanding of style guides, glossaries, terminology management, and localisation QA.

  • Experience working with localisation vendors or external linguists.

  • Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities.

  • Curiosity about AI and how it is changing localisation workflows.


We’d also love it if you have:

  • Previous experience as an in-house Language Manager or Language Lead.

  • Experience localising SaaS, consumer tech, or digital products.

  • Experience with CAT/TMS tools such as Smartling.

  • Experience with UX writing, copywriting, or transcreation.

  • Experience evaluating machine translation or LLM-generated content.

  • Familiarity with LQA or MQM frameworks.

  • Experience using data, user research, or product insights to inform localisation decisions.

  • Experience working with Product, Design, or Engineering teams.

  • A background in linguistics, translation, literature, localisation, or a related discipline.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Please note: This role requires the candidate to be based in Madrid or willing to relocate. We are open to candidates who have availability between 20-40 hours per week. 

 

About the Team

At Canva, we create tools that empower the world to design. Our mission is to democratize design and empower creativity for anyone and everyone, on every platform. Since launching in August 2013, Canva has grown exponentially—we're one of the world's fastest-growing startups, and the journey has only just begun.

International is becoming Canva's biggest growth driver in 2026 and beyond. To reach our foundational goal of having 1 in 5 internet users use Canva every month, we're shifting from translating English successes to implementing truly local strategies that resonate with and convert local audiences.

The LOX group spans the globe with keyword researchers, technical SEO specialists, content specialists, copywriters, engineers, data analysts, designers, and operations specialists. As SEO Outreach Specialist for Spain, you'll be part of the Logged Out Experience (LOX) Group and International Supergroup, working in a dual alignment model, embedded in your Country team locally while contributing to the global outreach team.

About the role

Link building is evolving fast: LLMs are changing how authority signals work, and what earned placements yesterday might not work tomorrow. This role requires someone who can balance proven tactics with experimentation, adapt quickly, and think beyond just securing backlinks.

You'll build high-quality backlinks for priority landing pages in Spain while exploring brand mention opportunities. You'll report to both your Spanish SEO Country Lead and the Global Outreach Lead, executing local strategy while contributing to global coordination.

As search evolves and LLM-driven discovery grows in importance, the most valuable authority signals will come from genuine earned coverage — not just link volume. This role is an early bet on that future, and the person who fills it will help define what modern outreach looks like for Spain.

This role combines three things:

  • Commercial outreach execution (your foundation): You know how to hit targets. You can build and manage a prospecting pipeline, write personalised outreach that gets responses, negotiate placements without paying for links, and maintain the kind of disciplined CRM hygiene that makes the whole operation compound over time. This is the foundation — and in the early months, it's where you'll build your credibility.

  • Editorial and PR thinking (your differentiator): Your editorial instinct is what sets you apart — you can look at Canva's data or a product moment and ask 'what's the story worth telling here?' You know how to pitch it to the right Spanish outlet and collaborate with the content team to make it publishable. At the same time, you stay plugged into Spain's marketing, community, and partnerships teams — amplifying their work, surfacing the link opportunities hidden inside it, and supporting your Country Lead on content or SEO tasks when priorities demand it.

  • Experimentation and global contribution (your growth path): You document what works and what doesn't. You run A/B tests on messaging, explore new platforms, use AI tools to automate the repetitive stuff so you can spend more time on the high-value work. And you share your findings with the global outreach team — because your insights on Spain's media ecosystem are genuinely valuable to a team operating across 20+ markets.

What makes this different from typical outreach roles:

You're not just executing a list handed to you. You're expected to be proactive, spotting opportunities, proposing optimizations, contributing to strategy discussions, and solving problems resourcefully. You'll operate with significant autonomy while staying aligned to your SEO Country Lead's priorities.

Success means delivering measurable authority growth that improves Canva's rankings and search visibility, helping more local users discover Canva and contributing to the country's market penetration goal.


What we're looking for

We're looking for an outreach specialist who thinks beyond the link. You have a solid foundation in digital PR or link building, a deep understanding of Spain's media and publisher landscape, and the curiosity to explore what earned authority looks like as search continues to evolve.

Spanish Market Expertise

  • Native Spanish speaker with business-level English (to collaborate globally and access English-language resources)

  • Deep understanding of Spain's digital publishing landscape, content creator ecosystem, and outreach norms

  • Familiarity with Spain's key media outlets — from tech and digital press to regional and institutional publications

  • Ability to identify locally relevant opportunities that non-locals would miss

Relationship Building & Communication

  • Positive, enthusiastic, and personable with excellent written communication skills

  • Proven ability to build authentic, trust-based relationships remotely — with publishers, editors, journalists, and content creators

  • Resilient in handling rejection — able to reframe conversations, identify alternative value exchanges, and negotiate win-win placements without paid links

  • Skilled at tailoring messaging for different audiences (journalists, bloggers, YouTubers, community moderators, institutional partners)

SEO or Marketing Experience

  • 1-2 years experience in link building, digital PR, content marketing, or related outreach-focused roles

  • Basic understanding of how search engines work and what makes a high-quality backlink

  • Familiarity with SEO tools (Ahrefs, Google Search Console, Screaming Frog) or willingness to learn quickly

AI Fluency & Technical Comfort

  • Comfortable using AI tools for drafting, research, and analysis

  • Basic understanding of how LLMs work and how they're changing content discovery

  • Not afraid of learning new software

Attention to Detail & Process Discipline

  • High attention to detail—able to closely follow detailed written instructions and quality standards

  • Organized and systematic in tracking outreach activity, managing contacts, and reporting progress

  • Comfortable working within structured frameworks while proposing improvements

Ownership & Proactive Mindset

  • You don't wait for instructions—you propose optimizations, identify opportunities, and solve problems resourcefully

  • You're comfortable with autonomy and accountability

  • You escalate strategically when blockers arise but default to solving problems yourself

Collaborative & Experimental Mindset

  • Thrives in a highly collaborative environment—both within the global SEO team and across country functions (marketing, community, PR)

  • Excited to embed with non-SEO teams and spot opportunities where outreach expertise adds value

  • Skilled at building trust across teams and making collaboration feel natural, not forced

  • Comfortable with experimentation, iteration, and occasional failure as part of the learning process

  • Curious and growth-oriented—always looking for ways to improve your craft and support others

Strategic Thinking (Growing Capability)

  • Ability to connect individual outreach campaigns to broader SEO goals

  • Comfortable participating in strategy discussions and contributing ideas

  • Willingness to step beyond pure execution and think about "why" not just "how"

Nice-to-Haves

  • Previous link building or digital PR experience

  • Experience creating content (blog posts, infographics, design assets) for outreach campaigns

  • Experience pitching to or working alongside journalists and editors

  • Basic design skills or comfort using Canva to create outreach assets

  • Experience with CRM (Pitchbox, BuzzStream)

  • Active participation in Spain's SEO, marketing, or content creator communities

 

We're setting a high bar—because International is becoming Canva's biggest growth driver, and we need exceptional people driving it.

What "A-Player" means in this role:

  • Strategic thinker: You define what should be done and why (not just execute)

  • Relationship builder: You make collaboration easy and productive — with publishers, editors, and internal teams alike

  • Problem solver: You're resourceful and resilient when challenges arise

  • Data-driven: You use insights to drive decisions and demonstrate impact

  • Ownership mindset: You act like it's your business, not just your job

  • Growth-oriented: You're constantly learning, adapting, and improving

To be successful in this role you must deeply understand the modern narrative formats of these channels, balance the art and science of creative and guide a small team where you will be very hands on. We take an iterative approach that is grounded in empathy and qualitative understanding of our market and customers as well as the metrics.

As part of this role, you will report to our Poland Marketing Lead and work collaboratively with the rest of the marketing team focused on brand campaigns, lifecycle and partnerships for example. You will help raise the bar in social content across the team.

What you’d be doing in this role

🧠 Own the end-to-end creative strategy and process

You'll lead the full creative cycle across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, and emerging channels. That means research, briefing, production, and performance review. You'll run sprint cycles with your pod, balancing quick-win iterations with bigger creative swings. Every sprint should build on the last and you bring insights to the broader creative team.

📊 Analyse and optimise creative performance

Dig into dashboards to spot what's winning, what's fatiguing, and why. Using cohort analysis uncover areas that work including but not limited to hooks, formats, messaging, creators and production sources. Feed those learnings directly back into the next sprint and strategy to keep the creative flywheel spinning.

🎥 Lead video editors, creators, and creative talent

Direct and collaborate with video editors, designers and writers to produce great work across formats. That includes short-form social, YouTube creative, creators, and any another paid assets. You'll brief and review creator content, build a network of local talent, and make sure everything is on brand, but built for the platform it's going on.

🤝 Partner with media buying and analytics

You'll work in lockstep with media buyers and our data science team. You need to understand how media buying influences creative success, and help the analytical side of the team understand the thinking behind creative decisions. This is about balancing the art and science of creative together.

👑 Champion the Polish market

You'll be the team's expert on the Polish market and cultural trends. Surface the cultural nuances, regional platform behaviours and translate that into creative that lands. As we scale across the EMEA region, you'll collaborate with creative strategists working on adjacent markets and partner closely with the broader marketing team across the entire funnel.

🤖 Accelerate workflows with AI and modern tools

Use AI tools to speed up ideation, research, asset generation, and analysis. Generate minimum viable concepts for prototypes and stay across emerging platforms, ad formats, and creative tech that give the team an edge.

🔄 Support conversion across the funnel

Drive CRO initiatives in partnership with our paid media expert to make acquisition journeys engaging and high converting. Your creative work should drive results across the full funnel, from awareness through to activation and retention.

You’re probably a match if you have:

  • You have solid experience in growth or performance marketing with a focus on creative strategy. You've worked hands on across Meta, TikTok, and YouTube creative.

  • Experience guiding creative talent. Video editors, designers, writers, or creators and coaching them to do great, performance-driven work.

  • A track record of partnering with media buying and analytics teams. You understand how both sides work and can bridge the gap between data and creative.

  • Confidence using creative analytics tools and performance dashboards to inform decisions and optimise creative at scale.

  • Strong creative instinct and pattern recognition. You know what makes a hook compelling, a format scroll-stopping, and a concept scalable across channels.

  • Fluent Polish and excellent English, with a sharp eye for tone, nuance, and cultural resonance in creative work.

  • Experience creating for the Polish market is essential.

  • Demonstrated ability to use AI tools to accelerate workflows and improve output quality

  • A portfolio of creative concepts you've personally shipped on Meta, TikTok, or YouTube. Walk us through the hook, the format, the result, and what you learned. We care about concept level thinking, not just one off ads.

  • Full proficiency in English and Polish (native or fluent Polish speaking and writing required).

About the team

You’ll be part of a highly collaborative, fast-moving, and passionate marketing team that blends creativity and data to make magic happen. In this role, you'll help Canva show up at its best in Poland and fuel growth by bringing performance and creativity together in every campaign.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora,你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point. 

What you'd be doing in this role:

Canva is making experimentation a much bigger part of how we build and ship product.

At our scale, shipping changes and watching what happens isn't enough. Teams need to know whether a change actually improved the product and catch changes that unexpectedly hurt important guardrails such as retention or application performance.

This Staff Software Engineer will provide senior technical leadership across the backend systems behind Canva's experimentation programme.

You'll help evolve the platform teams use to set up experiments, target users, expose variants and measure outcomes in the safest and most intuitive way possible. We're moving towards a platform that does more than report results. It should reinforce good experimentation practices, surface signals faster and alert early when things go wrong.

With the advent of AI, we’re also looking at how we can automate more of the analysis process to help our teams learn faster and iterate.

You'll take ownership of significant technical problems, work with senior leaders across Canva and help shape where the platform should go next by working with the teams building the platform.

You’re probably a match:

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience:

  • Backend platform engineering: You've built backend systems or platforms that other engineers depend on, and understand what changes when your software becomes part of somebody else's critical path.

  • Experimentation exposure at scale: You've built, operated or worked deeply with experimentation, A/B testing, feature-management or progressive-rollout systems in a large engineering environment.

  • Technical leadership: You've taken ambiguous engineering problems, formed a technical direction and helped other engineers move towards an outcome.

  • Driving adoption: You've built internal platforms or capabilities and understand that the technology only succeeds when other teams trust and use it.

Technical knowledge:

  • Backend and distributed systems: Strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience designing reliable backend systems and reasoning about scalability, availability, consistency and failure modes.

  • Data systems: Enough familiarity with data engineering, analytics engineering or large-scale data processing to understand how experimentation data is generated, moved and consumed.

  • Experimentation concepts: Familiarity with experiment assignment, targeting, variants, feature flags, metrics, guardrails and progressive rollout.

  • Language depth: Java is our primary language and would be useful, but it isn't a hard requirement. At Staff level, we're more interested in strong engineering fundamentals and your ability to transfer them between languages.

Nice to haves:

  • You've built this before: Direct experience designing or building experimentation, A/B testing, feature-management or rollout infrastructure — either inside a large technology company or for a platform vendor.

  • Data crossover: A background spanning software engineering and data science, data engineering or analytics engineering.

  • Feature flags: Experience building feature flagging, user targeting, progressive rollout or automated guardrail systems.

  • Statistical intuition: You don't need to be a data scientist, but being comfortable enough with experimentation and statistics to work closely with one will be valuable.

About the Group & Team:

This role sits within Rollout Insights, the subgroup responsible for experimentation at Canva.

The team builds shared experimentation capabilities used across the company.

Engineers use the platform to configure and launch experiments. Data scientists use the resulting data to understand impact. Product teams use those insights to decide what should roll out, change or stop.

The team already brings together software engineering and senior data science expertise, which matters because the hardest problems sit across both disciplines.

You'll also collaborate broadly across Canva's engineering and data science organisations, including with senior technical leaders who depend on the platform.

Experimentation is now a major company priority, so demand for the team's capabilities is growing quickly. There's already a platform to build from, with plenty of important technical work still ahead.
